The image rows also carry docs/02 §6's "never receives" words (`NEVER_RECEIVES_NOTES`). With nothing reserved, the Reserved section says so in one line.
  **Why:** the guide is generated in code and has no template file to copy. The format line is that template.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** the planned test names change to IDs the traceability gate knows: `test_not_configured` becomes `test_i_23__m8_not_configured`, `test_image_adapter_registration` becomes `test_i_23__m8_adapter_registration`, and `test_image_config_secret` becomes `test_c_09__m8_image_key`. All three live in `tests/integration/test_images_config.py`, because one part ID and milestone may come from one file only. docs/04 §15's NFR-SEC-3 row gains `C-09 (M8)`. `test_i_24__m8_data_flow_rows` and `test_c_04__m8_image` keep their planned names.
  **Why:** `check-traceability` reads a part's ID from the test's name, and a bare name such as `NOT-CONFIGURED` is no docs/04 test. docs/04 I-23 opens with exactly the not-configured clause.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** the M2 part `test_c_04` keeps the M8 lexicon out of its text. Its path expectation for own-row purposes is computed from `registry.OWN_ROW_ONLY` and `suite.OWN_ROW_PATH`, and the shared conformance suite (and C-09's `exercise`) give `image_check` a row of its own, because it inherits no endpoint.
  **Why:** `check-lexicon` refused "image check" and "image prompt" in an M2 part. The suite calls every delivered purpose under the `openai` adapter, and an unset `image_check` is `not_configured`.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** `model_matrix.run_matrix` assesses the delivered purposes except `OWN_ROW_ONLY` ones.
  **Why:** the matrix points only `default` at the target, so `image_check` would always report incapable. The matrix's table lists story purposes only.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** `Port` is generic over its floor (`Port[EmbeddingFloor]`, `Port[ImageGenerationFloor]`; `PortFloor` is the union), and `CapabilityFloor` gains `vision: bool`, which is declared and never probed.
  **Why:** the replan widened `Port.floor` per port. Making `Port` generic keeps `EMBEDDING.floor.max_batch` typed for the embedding service. "PUT on `image_check` records the vision floor; no probe" means the registry declares the floor.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** no migration. The image config is the existing `model_config` row `image_generation`, and alembic head stays `0131_backfill_inferred_states`.
  **Why:** the planner's Discretion says there is no new table.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** the reserved-purpose refusal tests use `tests/model_support.py::reserved_purpose(monkeypatch)`, which declares `future_purpose` (M10) in `registry.RESERVED_PURPOSES`, `registry.RESERVED`, `access.RESERVED` and the package's re-export.
  **Why:** the replan (M6 #199) keeps the reserved machinery covered once M8 empties it.
  **Issue:** #254
- **Decision:** #255 adds three defaulted fields to #254's port: `ImageOutput.width` and `ImageOutput.height` (read by Pillow from the returned bytes), `SubmitResult.applied_parameters` (a new `port.AppliedParameters`: `{endpoint, requested, sent, seed_applied, references_applied, negative_prompt, dropped_parameters}`), and `ImageAdapterConfig.references`. Without them the adapter would have no place to return what it actually applied or the dimensions it decoded. `seed_applied` and `references_applied` are `None` when nothing of that kind was requested. `sent` records references as a count, never as URLs. Every name is the wire name (`input_references`, not `reference_images`).
  **Why:** the AC puts `applied_parameters` and the decoded dimensions on the attempt, and #256 records the attempt from `SubmitResult`. The fields are additive, so the stubs and #254's tests are unchanged.
  **Issue:** #255, #256
- **Decision:** reference images resolve through `orchestrator/images/references.py`. It holds `ReferenceResolver`, plus `MediaReferences(db, store, signer)`, which the Engine sets on `models.images.references` and the registry passes in `ImageAdapterConfig.references`. A #107 signed URL is used when the provider can fetch its host; any other case gets a data URL of at most 1024 px and 4 MiB, in the stored type. "Can fetch" means http(s), not `localhost`/`*.localhost`/`*.local`/`*.internal`/a dotless name, and not a private, loopback, link-local, reserved, multicast or unspecified IP. Host names are not resolved. A missing asset, or one that is not an image, is `ImageRequestInvalid`. An adapter with no resolver drops the references (`references_applied: false`), and they never narrow routing.
  **Why:** the planner's single-module line is about the adapter. Every hosted adapter needs reference resolution, and the factory signature is `factory(config)`, so the resolver travels in the config.
  **Issue:** #255
- **Decision:** `tests/integration/test_images_config.py` is renamed to `tests/integration/test_i_23.py` (`git mv`), and #255's I-23 parts are added to it. Those parts are `test_i_23__m8_openrouter_contract`, `_capability_cache`, `_errors`, `_recorded` and `_dedupe_flag`. The planned `test_openrouter_dedupe_flag` carries the `test_i_23__m8_` prefix.
  **Why:** the traceability gate takes one file per test ID and milestone, and the replan names `test_i_23.py` as I-23's M8 file. #254 had put its two I-23 parts in `test_images_config.py`. A part name without a docs/04 ID is "unmappable". Renaming now saves every later I-23 story (#259, #261, #263…) from the same choice.
  **Issue:** #255, #254
- **Decision:** the adapter parses endpoint records tolerantly, because the public docs do not show the endpoints answer in full. The list may sit at `data.endpoints`, `data` or `endpoints`. `supported_parameters` may be a list, or a mapping keyed by name as the models list uses. The slug is the first of `tag`, `provider_slug`, `slug`, `provider_name` or `name`, and a response's `provider` matches any of them case-insensitively. Reference images go as `{"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": …}}`, OpenRouter's published shape. The endpoints-API path and the models-list path are `/api/v1/images/models/{id}/endpoints` and `/api/v1/images/models`.
  **Why:** the owner's recording confirms the real shape. Accepting the plausible shapes means the recorded fixtures should need no code change. If a field is named differently, the change is one line in `SLUG_FIELDS` or `parse_endpoints`.
  **Issue:** #255
- **Decision:** routing details beyond the planner lines. `n` is sent only when it is above 1 and a chosen endpoint lists it; otherwise it is dropped and recorded. After the call, a sent parameter that the serving endpoint does not list joins `dropped_parameters`. The serving endpoint is the response's `provider`, else the single chosen endpoint (covering both the single `only` slug and a model with one endpoint), else `null`. A discovery 401/403/404/zero-endpoints error is never masked by a stale cache entry, but a 5xx, timeout or malformed answer is. A connect timeout is `ImageProviderTimeout(ambiguous=False)`, because nothing was sent. A transport error after connecting is `ImageProviderUnavailable(ambiguous=True)`.
  **Why:** the planner says to judge applied parameters against the serving endpoint, and to judge ambiguity by whether the send could have reached the provider (#268).
  **Issue:** #255, #268
- **Decision:** the recorder makes exactly six calls (`CALL_BUDGET`, enforced by its recording transport): the list, the endpoints, a plain call with key K, a seeded call, a reference call, and the plain call again with K. The AC's "the same request twice" counts the plain call as the first of the pair. The recorded fixtures go to `tests/fixtures/openrouter/recorded/<nn>_<name>.json`, beside `verdict.json`, not loose in `tests/fixtures/openrouter/`. That lets the atomic write rename one directory without touching `synthetic/` or `ref.png`. The verdict's dedupe check follows the planner literally: `dedupes: true` only when the repeat answered the same generation id, and otherwise `dedupes: false, inconclusive: true`. Ids are redacted consistently (the same value gets the same `REDACTED-<n>`), so the committed fixtures still show the dedupe evidence. A model-list `id` is kept, and only a generation's top-level `id` is redacted.
  **Why:** the six-call budget, and the planner's recorder lines.
  **Issue:** #255
- **Decision:** the recorder was not run against openrouter.ai. `OPENROUTER_DEDUPES_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` stays `False`. `test_i_23__m8_openrouter_recorded` and `_dedupe_flag` skip until `verdict.json` exists (reason `needs-owner-action`). A simulated recording, made by the recorder against the replay server and then deleted, made both pass with no code change. The recording AC box stays unticked, and the story stays open with `needs-owner-action`.
  **Why:** the run needs the owner's key and spend (round one). The owner commits the fixtures and sets the constant from the verdict, in the same PR.
  **Issue:** #255
- **Decision:** the `image_generation` entry's `endpoint` reads `openrouter.ai` when `base_url` is null and the adapter is `openrouter` (`params.ADAPTER_DEFAULT_BASE_URLS`, `default_base_url`). Pillow was already a runtime dependency (#105, `pillow>=13.0.0`), so no install was needed, and `check-licenses` passes.
  **Why:** #254's decision left `endpoint` null "until #255 knows OpenRouter's default".
  **Issue:** #255, #254
- **Decision:** #256's planned bare test names are given test IDs the traceability gate knows. The FR-IMG-3 ones are C-22 parts in `tests/conformance/test_c_22.py`: `test_c_22__m8_fail_closed`, `test_c_22__m8_require_checker` (planned `test_require_image_checker`) and `test_c_22__m8_retry_budget` (planned `test_image_job_retry_budget`). The FR-IMG-4 ones are I-25 parts in `tests/integration/test_i_25.py`: `test_i_25__m8_idempotent`, `_long_poll` and `_outside_turn_budget`, plus `_cancel` for the Read AC's cancel. I-25's crash clauses get a part of their own, `test_i_25__m8_crash_sweeps` (FR-IMG-3), beside `test_i_25__m8_staging`. `test_x_07__m8_staging` keeps its name.
  **Why:** `check-parts` reports a part whose name maps to no docs/04 ID as unmappable. #254 made the same rename, and docs/04 §15 already lists I-25 (M8) and C-22 (M8) for FR-IMG-3,4.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** `image_output_policy_set` always counts the seeded minors policy (`minors_no_sexual_content`) as applying to image outputs while it exists, whatever its `applies_to` says. Other live global policies count when they name `image_output`.
  **Why:** the AC says "the seeded minors policy always does", but its `applies_to` gains the image targets only in #257's migration. Counting it now keeps `require_image_checker` and the fail-closed rule honest before #257. A deployment that deletes the policy loses it, as FR-GUARD-11 allows.
  **Issue:** #256, #257
- **Decision:** the checks seam (`ImageChecks`, `set_image_checks`) defaults to `FailClosedChecks` until #257 and #258 land. Every prompt passes (the prompt check is #257's). An output with no applicable policy stays `unchecked`. With `image_check` unset, the check raises `ImageCheckUnconfigured`. With `image_check` configured it raises `ImageCheckUnavailable`, because no output check is delivered yet, so nothing can pass. Tests and the fault harness install `testing.images.ScriptedChecks`.
  **Why:** fail closed. No production route enqueues a job before #260/#263, and an output check that ignored the image would pass anything.
  **Issue:** #256, #257, #258
- **Decision:** `DELETE /image-jobs/{job_id}` is flagged `route_flags(mutating=False)` and named in `tests/replay_support.UNKEYED_WRITES`. It still requires the principal, but it takes no `Idempotency-Key` and answers `ImageJobBody` with no `config_revision`. Cancelling a queued job also finishes its #70 `jobs` row as `done` with `result {"image_job": "cancelled"}`.
  **Why:** a cancel is idempotent by design (a terminal job answers unchanged), which is the rule the other unkeyed writes follow (docs/02 §9). A keyed route would need `DeploymentMutationResponse`'s `config_revision`, which a cancel does not change. `jobs.status` has no `cancelled` value, and widening that CHECK is a schema change the AC does not ask for.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** the after-commit staging deletes run after each ending transaction's `begin()` block exits, inside the pipeline (`end_job`, `cancel_job`, promotion). A failed delete is logged by class name and left to `image_staging_sweep`. They do not use #45's Operation hook list.
  **Why:** the job's transitions are plain transactions, not Operations, and `Operation` has no general after-commit hook list (only its summary notification). The effect is the same: the delete happens only once the ending has committed.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** `image_reservations` has the primary key `(job_id, attempt_token)`, which is the AC's uniqueness, and a `created_at` column to order attempts. `image_jobs.attempts` counts attempts that were sent: it is incremented in the transaction that marks the attempt `sending`. CHECKs added: `(story_id IS NOT NULL) = (kind = 'story')` and `attempts >= 0`, beside the AC's three.
  **Why:** "`attempts` counts reservation rows (a crash reclaim adds none until a new send)". A prepared row that was never sent cost nothing.
  **Issue:** #256, #262
- **Decision:** until #268, a reclaimed run resumes as follows. A current attempt still `prepared` is sent. An attempt in `checking` with its outputs still staged has only its checks re-run on those bytes (this is also the path for checker retries). Any other attempt is discarded with its staged bytes (`sending` → `ambiguous`, outcome `discarded`), and a new attempt starts under a new token without waiting for a horizon.
  **Why:** provider delivery is at least once and promotion at most once. #268 replaces the last branch with idempotent re-sends and presumed settlement.
  **Issue:** #256, #267, #268
- **Decision:** a retryable adapter error marks the attempt `failed`, moves the job back to `queued` under a new token, and raises `ImageJobRetry`, so #70's `fail_job` backs off. On the last try (`failures + 1 >= job_max_attempts`, carried in `ImageRuntime.max_attempts`), the job ends `failed`/`provider_unavailable` instead. A checker failure follows the same pattern and ends `image_check_unavailable`.
  **Why:** the planner's provider-error and checker-unavailable lines. Without the last-try rule, `jobs` would end `failed` while `image_jobs` stayed in `generating`.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** `image_worker_concurrency` is enforced in the worker as `WorkerConfig.kind_caps = {"image_job": N}`. A loop takes a capped kind's slot before it claims (with no `await` between the count and the take), and `queue.claim(exclude_kinds=...)` skips a kind that is at its cap.
  **Why:** `claim` takes the earliest due job of any kind, so a cap has to filter the claim. Taking the slot first keeps loops racing in one process from going over the cap.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** the crash tests run `images.after_stage` and `images.promote.before_commit` as process crashes in a child engine: `EngineProcess(images=True, config_key=...)`, a new `faults serve --images` option. It registers `testing.images.PngImageGenerator` as `faults_png`, the test target for `story`, and passing checks. "The job then ended by recovery" is simulated in SQL (`failed`/`interrupted`, with its `jobs` row): an ending that committed and died before its after-commit delete, which is exactly the case the staging sweep exists for.
  **Why:** the replan's crash convention. #256's own endings delete staging at once, so a sweep test needs an ending whose delete never ran.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** `test_i_25__m8_outside_turn_budget`'s respond hook monkeypatches `Operation.commit` in the test to add a commit step that calls `insert_image_job` for `turn` operations. There is no production seam.
  **Why:** the planner calls for a test-only hook, removed when #265 lands. The respond path has no hook list, and adding one would be production code for a test.
  **Issue:** #256, #265
- **Decision:** what a run does with outputs. Outputs beyond the requested `n` are discarded unchecked. Bytes that do not sniff and decode as an image (Pillow `verify`) are discarded unchecked and are not violations. If no usable output remains, the job ends `provider_empty_result`. Each staged output is fsynced. Promotion copies the passing bytes to a sibling file and `put`s that copy, so a fenced attempt's staging stays intact for its ending's delete. A promote that finds its staging gone treats the attempt as fenced. `generation_metadata.endpoint` is the adapter-reported serving endpoint. `applied_parameters` add `seed` and `seed_source` (`requested`/`engine`). The request's `caption` and `alt_text` are kept in `image_jobs.params` beside the six planned keys, because the promoted asset carries them and #257 checks them.
  **Why:** the AC, the planner's gate default for empty results, and the cancel race found while testing: a released worker used to crash with `FileNotFoundError` after the cancel deleted its staging (Rule 1, fixed, covered by `test_i_25__m8_cancel`).
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** `tests/api_surface_support.CURRENT` moves to `M8`. `PENDING` names the eight M8 `not_yet` rows still to come, each with its story: #259 `/image-prompts`, #260 the five catalog candidate routes, #261/#263 `POST /stories/{id}/images`, #261 the story-image delete. The planned API also gains an `images` OpenAPI tag (C-01 requires every operation to carry a known tag).
  **Why:** #256 flips the first M8 rows to `present`, and `test_c_15__api_surface` refuses a `present` row from a milestone after `CURRENT`. This is the same mechanism M7 used for its in-progress rows. It is independent of `pyproject`'s `current_milestone`, which stays at 7 until #271 (the run's decision).
  **Issue:** #256, #259, #260, #261, #263
- **Decision:** `image_retry_budget` and `staging_ttl` are a new deployment settings section (`ImageJobSettings`, both prospective) with their `SettingsPatch` fields. S-DELETE plants an `image_jobs` row, and `test_a_write_keeps_every_other_section` stores a non-default `image_retry_budget`.
  **Why:** the planner's Settings line. `test_u_18` requires the REST patch to name every setting, and both tests require every story table and every settings section to be exercised.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision (Rule 3):** CI run 42363214190 found five registries the first commit missed. `image_jobs` joins `determinism.OPERATIONAL_TABLES` (work in progress, with random attempt tokens). `image_jobs` and `image_reservations` join the subject index's `EXEMPT_TABLES`, with the reason that indexing and redacting a job's prompt is #266's, along with the images. `Engine.get_image_job` takes `wait` and `since_status` keyword-only, so the NUL-refusal check reports them as `query.*`. `cancel_image_job` is not `refuses_nul`, because no mutation is: a `job_id` that is no ULID is 404 before any query. `test_i_25__m8_crash_sweeps` asserts the rolled-back promotion by its orphan's checksum, not by a `media_assets` count, because the child's own media sweep runs against the shared database.
  **Why:** these registries (`test_determinism`, `test_every_content_table_has_a_writer`, `test_nul_text`) aren't in the touched-area tests I ran locally. CI's full sharded run is the gate that catches them.
  **Issue:** #256, #266
- **Decision:** process note. The plan comment on #256 was posted after the exploration and the first code, not before it.
  **Why:** honesty about the n8-exec order. The plan the comment gives is the one implemented.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** #257 step 0. CI run 42365801989 on `e948220` (#256's final commit) ended green on every job, so there is no Rule 1 fix under #256.
  **Why:** the brief asked for the check before #257's code. The only jobs still running at the start were the evals and zero-leak runs, and all of them passed.
  **Issue:** #256
- **Decision:** #257's figure classification is a `figures` variant of `guardrail_check`. It uses the template `guardrail_figures.j2` and the response schema `FigureClassification` (`{figures: [{descriptor, classification}], subjects: [{label, visual_descriptors}]}`). The schema is keyed to the stub by its template (`stub_script`), so no policy-check script answers it. The call runs once per prompt, and only when some age-conditioned policy targets `image_prompt`. Any `ModelError`, or an `Uncertain` after #53's retries, counts as one indeterminate figure (`UNRESOLVED_FIGURE`).
  **Why:** the planner says "a new response schema under `guardrail_check`". The `subjects` half is the planner's "the classification call returns descriptors for figures and named characters". With no age-conditioned policy in play, a figure's class can change no outcome, so the call would be pure cost.
  **Issue:** #257
- **Decision:** `ImageSubject` gains `classification` (adult, minor or indeterminate) and an optional `true_age`, which is `None` for a figure. `guardrail_check` receives `CheckedImageSubject`, a subclass that adds `mentioned_as`: the texts' own spans for the subject. Only the figure classification fills `mentioned_as`, so the model can leave resolved subjects out. `image_check` keeps the plain `ImageSubject`. `image_check.j2` now renders a figure as its class, and #258 inherits that. The model guide is regenerated.
  **Why:** a figure has no true age. The classifier can't tell "Lily" in the prompt from `subject_1` without the prompt's own word for her, and FR-IMG-13 allows that because it is no name the prompt lacks. A policy check needs none of it, so its payload stays exactly FR-IMG-13's list.
  **Issue:** #257, #258
- **Decision:** a refusal uses the text input's envelope (`policies.check.guardrail_violation`, message "Image prompt violates N policies: a minor is involved or present."). Each violation's key is `name`, not the AC's `policy_name`. Every applicable policy is evaluated, model-assisted ones included, even after a deterministic violation, so the error lists every violated policy.
  **Why:** FR-IMG-3 says "the policy error, as for text input", and FR-GUARD-10's shipped error says `name`. Two spellings of one error would be worse. The AC asks for every violated policy, and that costs the extra calls.
  **Issue:** #257
- **Decision:** the texts checked are the prompt, negative prompt, caption and alt text, each labelled on its own line for a model call. Deterministic policies run on each text separately, so a label can never match a word list.
  **Why:** the AC's check_prompt line names the negative prompt. FR-IMG-13 says "the image prompt", and the negative prompt is part of it.
  **Issue:** #257
- **Decision:** resolution details. A name part two characters share ("Ann" for Ann Lee and Ann Moss) resolves to both. Erasure's `with_name_parts` leaves shared parts out, so the safety path adds back every part of a character's own name. A declared id may be the character's own, its persona's or its catalog character's, and an id the target doesn't know is 422 `validation_error` at `body.depicted_subjects[i]`. A known character with no age on record (a catalog draft) is indeterminate. A subject found several ways keeps the first source in this order: declared or depicted, then named, then present.
  **Why:** safety fails closed, the reverse of erasure's trade-off. An unknown declared id is a client error, not a figure.
  **Issue:** #257
- **Decision:** presence. An origin with no `position` uses the end of its turn and variant, with every beat's moves (`POSITION_MAX`). A slot `N⁺k` uses `load_scene_state(N+1)`, the scene after turn N and its slots. The actors passed to `turn_audience` are the image's viewpoint, when it is a character, and the resolved subjects, as #541's actors are. Anything a consumer sends as a roster is ignored.
  **Why:** the planner says "a slot uses the scene at the end of turn N". The union over a turn's states errs toward applying the policy, as `placed_elsewhere` does.
  **Issue:** #257
- **Decision:** `ImageJobRequest.depicted_subjects` is a list of `DepictedSubject{character_id, visual_descriptors, depicted}`, and a bare id string is accepted. The list is not copied into `image_jobs.params`. The resolved context goes to the new `image_jobs.safety_context` (jsonb, nullable), which no view returns. `ImageChecks.check_prompt` now returns the `SafetyContext`, and `prepare_image_job` keeps it on `PreparedImageJob`. The default `FailClosedChecks.check_prompt` is the real check, and `safety_checks.PromptChecks(output)` pairs it with any output check, as the tests use it. `PromptCheck` gains `principal` and `viewpoint`.
  **Why:** FR-IMG-9 says requests declare their subjects, and #259/#263 will send them. The planner puts the context in `image_jobs.safety_context` with character ids. #258 reads it for the output check.
  **Issue:** #257, #258, #259, #263
- **Decision:** migration `0133_minors_image_targets` unions `image_prompt` and `image_output` into the seeded policy's `applies_to`. It runs silently, as `0009` did: no `config_changes` row and no version bump. An edited policy keeps its own targets, and a removed one is skipped. The migration also adds `image_jobs.safety_context` and the audit kind `image_prompt_rejected`, whose details hold the target's kind and id, the entry point and the subject and figure counts. `MINORS_POLICY` keeps its two text targets, because it is the row `0009` inserts, and the new `IMAGE_TARGETS` names what `0133` adds. `test_seed_row` now expects all four. The admin API already accepted image targets on rating policies (`schemas.Targets` is the full enum), so no code change was needed. `test_c_22__m8_prompt` creates such a policy and sees it enforced.
  **Why:** the planner's migration line and the seed module's own rule ("change seeds through a new migration").
  **Issue:** #257
- **Decision:** the catalog path is built ahead of #260. A character entry's own character is always a subject (`depicted`, FR-IMG-9), with the draft's age as written. A scenario entry's locked and default role characters are the universe, each read at its pinned version, else its current version, else its draft. The entry's rating joins the global policies (`creation_context`).
  **Why:** the AC's catalog clause ("global ∪ the entry's rating", "`catalog_true_age`"). #260 wires the route and its tests. `test_catalog_image_subjects` covers the character entry.
  **Issue:** #257, #260
- **Decision:** test names and files. The planned `test_figure_classification_fail_closed` is `test_i_24__m8_figure_classification_fail_closed`. #254's `test_i_24__m8_data_flow_rows` moved from `tests/test_images_port.py` into the new `tests/integration/test_i_24.py`, because `check-traceability` refused I-24's M8 parts in two files. The gate test `tests/gates/test_image_paths_contract.py` and the unit-level `tests/integration/test_image_safety_context.py` carry no part marker. The planned "whisper-scene fixture" did not exist, so `tests/image_safety_support.py` builds that cast (Bobby, Jenni, Marcus 34, Lily 17 and Wren 16) from test constants.
  **Why:** a part whose name maps to no docs/04 ID is unmappable, and the traceability gate takes one file per test ID and milestone.
  **Issue:** #257, #254
- **Decision:** `docs/evals/INDEX.md` is regenerated. Lite is now `2e85109a0c24`, Standard `443af45359e2`, Full `7f7956250424` and Max `492736d820b9`, and all four read uncertified as before. The edit to `guardrail_check.j2` and the new `guardrail_figures.j2` variant moved `TEMPLATE_HASHES`. `evals --check` and `evals index --check` pass. No committed record was edited.
  **Why:** the Fingerprint move AC, following #760's precedent.
  **Issue:** #257, #760
- **Decision:** #258's multimodal message is `Message.images: tuple[str, ...]` (image URLs carried after the text), not a `content: str | parts` union. `Message.wire()` sends `{role, content}` unchanged for a text message and OpenAI's content array (`text`, then one `image_url` part per image) when there are images. `openai_compatible.request_body`, the stub's digest, `lite.prompt.prompt_hash` and the model probe all send `wire()`, which is byte-identical to the old `model_dump()` for text messages, and the held-call key adds images only when present. `prompts.render` attaches every top-level input field tagged `ContentCategory.IMAGE` (`ImageCheckInputs.image`) to the last user message, so no template ever renders an image as text.
  **Why:** a union on `content` broke 60 call sites in 39 files, most of them tests reading `.content` as text. A separate field gives the same wire shape with no change for any text purpose, and no fingerprint or prompt hash moves.
  **Issue:** #258
- **Decision:** no `policies.on_uncertain` column. The AC says "if absent", and #49's `rule.on_uncertain` already holds it (`violation`/`pass`). The output check reads it as `violation` → `block` and `pass` → `allow`. The seeded minors policy's rule is `violation`, so it blocks on all four targets. A deterministic policy is never uncertain.
  **Why:** a second column would be a second source of truth for the same setting, and every policy writer, fork copy and export would have to keep them in step.
  **Issue:** #258, #49
- **Decision:** the output check judges every image-output policy, age-conditioned ones included, whether or not a subject is a minor. This differs from the prompt check, which gates an age-conditioned policy on `has_minor`. The seeded minors policy always applies to outputs while it exists (#256's rule), so any configured checker checks every image. A character policy applies only for a resolved subject.
  **Why:** the checker judges what the image shows, and it can show a minor that nobody named. A backstop gated on the prompt's subjects would only repeat the prompt check.
  **Issue:** #258
- **Decision:** reading the checker's answer. An omitted id or `uncertain` counts as uncertain. So does an answer that never validates after #53's retries (`Uncertain`), for every model-assisted policy. Each then follows `on_uncertain`. A `ModelError` is unavailability: in a job, `ImageCheckUnavailable` (retried on the same bytes, then `image_check_unavailable`); on an upload, 503 `image_check_unavailable`. The call's budget is `TurnBudget(deadline_s=180)`, and the per-call timeout comes from the purpose's params (default 60 s). `structured_call` takes no deterministic step (`lambda: None`), because deterministic policies run locally first.
  **Why:** the AC, and #257's precedent for `Uncertain` (it takes `on_uncertain`). A garbled answer is the checker's judgement failing, not the checker being down.
  **Issue:** #258
- **Decision:** an upload's safety context (`core.images.safety.build_upload_safety_context`) holds the declared subjects with their true ages. A story character's age is its current one at the story's head, a catalog character's is the age as written, and a persona's is its `age`. A declared id that does not exist yet is indeterminate, so it counts as a minor. The context also holds every catalog character or persona that the caption or alt text names (`index.catalog_subjects`, candidate mentions included). An undeclared story character named in a caption is not resolved: an upload has no story, so there is no story universe to search. The applicable policies are the global ones, the rating's (`creation_context`) and the character policies of the declared story characters.
  **Why:** the planner's lines. Uploads may declare subjects created later (#105), and safety fails closed.
  **Issue:** #258
- **Decision:** an upload refusal uses the text input's envelope (`guardrail_violation`, each violation `{policy_id, name, message}`, "Image violates N policies: a minor is involved or present."). The AC asked for `policy_name`, and #257 made the same call for prompts. The `image_upload_rejected` audit row (new kind, migration 0134) holds `{entry_point: media_upload, operation_id}` and the policy ids. Its `operation_id` is the upload's staged asset id: the would-be asset id, which a refusal never stores. It holds no image and no hash. The audit row commits on its own, so it survives the upload's rollback.
  **Why:** one error shape for one error (FR-GUARD-10). A refused upload creates no operation row, and the staged id is the only id the request has minted.
  **Issue:** #258, #257
- **Decision:** the image check runs on images only: an image upload, a video's `poster_file` and an extracted poster. A refused poster refuses the video. A video itself is stored `unchecked`, and so is a poster that names an existing asset (that asset carries its own check). The check runs after the probe and before the moderation hook, in both `POST /media` and a resumable upload's completion. The completion's check runs inside its row-locked transaction, as the hook already does.
  **Why:** the `image_check` purpose is a vision model for images (FR-IMG-3), and the AC says posters follow the image rule.
  **Issue:** #258
- **Decision:** `check_endpoint` is the host of the checker's `base_url`, or the adapter's name (`stub`, `openai`) when none is set, because the CHECK needs a non-null value on a `passed` row. `checker_fingerprint` is computed over that host, or `null` when no `base_url` is set, never over the adapter name. `reported_version` comes from `reported_version.latest`, which is keyed by model id only. The template hash is the SHA-256 of the shipped `image_check.j2` (`output_check.TEMPLATE_SHA256`).
  **Why:** the AC's definition (#270/#271 reuse it), and `latest()`'s existing shape.
  **Issue:** #258, #270, #271
- **Decision:** `image_check_certifications` is `(id, checker_fingerprint 12-hex CHECK, policy_id, policy_version, model_id, metrics jsonb, report_sha256, recorded_at, recorded_via job|import, status valid|stale)`, indexed on `(checker_fingerprint, policy_id, status)`. The lookup is `core.profiles.certification.image_check_certified(conn, fingerprint, policy_ids)`, where a `valid` row means certified. `OutputChecks` caches the lookup per job (an LRU of 256). The table is in the subject index's `EXEMPT_TABLES`.
  **Why:** the AC gives `(id, checker_fingerprint, policy_id, …)`. The rest mirrors `profile_certifications` closely enough for #270 to record E-11 runs without another migration.
  **Issue:** #258, #270
- **Decision:** the default checks stay `jobs.FailClosedChecks`, which now delegates `check_output` to `output_check.OutputChecks`. A job's policies are the target's effective set (`safety_checks.target_policies`), read with the job's stored `SafetyContext`. A story deleted mid-job falls back to the global policies, and promotion then ends the job `target_gone`. `insert_output_asset` writes the verdict's check fields, and it takes `source` (default `generated`) so #263 can mark consumer prompts `generated_from_consumer_prompt`.
  **Why:** #256's seam. Every test that installs `ScriptedChecks` is unchanged. The source belongs to the target, which knows who wrote the prompt.
  **Issue:** #258, #256, #263
- **Decision:** reads. `MediaAsset` gains `check_status` and `check` (`ImageCheck{model, endpoint, policies: [PolicyCheck{policy_id, policy_version, name, result, certified}]}`, `null` unless `passed`), built from the stored columns. The read types and the two statements live in the new `core/media/checks.py`, so `core.catalog.models` can import them without pulling in `core.media.assets`. Catalog `full`'s `CharacterImageDetail` gains `source`, `check_status` and `check`. The statements are in the descriptions of `MediaAsset` (and `MediaUploadedBody`), `ImageCheck` and `CharacterImageDetail`, and in the `POST /media` description. `StoryImage` and `ImageCandidate` do not exist yet: #261/#260 reuse `ImageCheck` and the statements.
  **Why:** the AC's read schema is "one pydantic model with optional `check`".
  **Issue:** #258, #260, #261
- **Decision:** test names and files. The planned `test_upload_check_payload` (FR-IMG-13) is `test_i_24__m8_upload_check_payload` in `tests/integration/test_i_24.py`. C-24's part is split into `test_c_24__m8_metadata`, `_certified` and `_statements` in the new `tests/conformance/test_c_24.py`, all `part("M8", "FR-IMG-10")`. I-24's "true ages reach the image checker" clause gets its own part, `test_i_24__m8_checker_true_ages` (FR-IMG-12,13). `tests/test_output_check.py` is unit-level and carries no part marker or requirement ID. Its first draft named FR-PROF-16 in a docstring, which made it an M3 part and failed check-lexicon, so the ID was removed. `test_media_tables` and `test_full_inlines_each_image_and_the_card_never_does` now expect the new columns and fields.
  **Why:** the traceability gate maps part names to docs/04 IDs, one file per ID and milestone. The brief warns that a requirement ID in a docstring makes the test a part.
  **Issue:** #258
- **Decision (Rule 1):** `test_i_24__m8_two_paths` (#257) asserted that "34" appears nowhere in the generator's request JSON. That JSON holds a random engine seed, and one local run failed on seed `1315043446`. The assertion now dumps the request without `seed`, and #258's `_checker_true_ages` does the same. The prompt and every other field are still checked.
  **Why:** a 10-digit random seed contains "34" in about a quarter of runs, so the test was a flake. The seed is never derived from an age.
  **Issue:** #258, #257
- **Decision:** #259's canon half is `core/images/perceived.py`. It does more than the planner's `catalog_perceived_inputs`: it also holds `resolve_target` (draft, version or latest; 404 and `not_published`), `entry_document`, `read_perceived`, and the base-prompt inputs `base_appearance_inputs`/`BaseAppearanceInputs`, which keeps the true age and the restricted terms inside its `leaks` check. `orchestrator/images/prompt_builder.py` imports only `perceived`, so the import contract `images-generation-path-has-no-ages` holds with `prompt_builder` added. Its gate test checks the new source and adds a copy whose builder imports `core.images.safety`. The band is #170's `age_band` over `catalog_true_age`, unchanged. The "unknown third → mid" rule can never apply to a catalog entry's own true age, so it is left to #263's perceived ages.
  **Why:** the planner's pass-2 split. Keeping the true age in Core, even for the drafted-text check, means no age value ever enters the Orchestrator's image path.
  **Issue:** #259, #263
- **Decision:** the route's body and answer models (`ImagePromptRequest`, `ImagePromptTarget`, `BuiltImagePrompt`, `ResolvedTarget`, `BaseAppearanceRequest`, `DraftedBaseAppearance`) live in `orchestrator/images/prompt_builder.py`, not in `api/routes/image_prompts.py`. The route module imports them.
  **Why:** the planner wants `Engine.build_image_prompt` to take the route's shape, and the Engine imports nothing from `epistrel.api`.
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** a version build's safety context reads that version. `SafetyRequest` gains `entry_version`, and `_catalog_candidates` reads `character_versions`/`scenario_versions` content when it is set. `safety_request` takes it from a catalog origin's `version`. Before this change, a catalog context always read the draft.
  **Why:** Rule 1. #257's module docstring already says "a catalog image uses the version's age as written". A prompt built from version 1 must be judged by version 1's age and rating, not by a later draft's.
  **Issue:** #259, #257, #260
- **Decision:** the output schema `ImagePromptResult` is now `{prompt}` only (1 to 2,000 characters, never blank). #254's `negative_prompt` output field is gone, since the negative prompt is deterministic and never passes through the model. `ImagePromptSubject.description` widens to 4,000 characters (a catalog appearance's own bound) and `visual_style` to 2,000 (the scenario's style bound). `image_prompt` is not story-scoped, so no preset fingerprint moves, and `evals --check` and `evals index --check` pass. `docs/models.md` is regenerated.
  **Why:** the AC (output `{prompt}`) and the planner's output line. The input bounds had been set before the catalog bounds were known.
  **Issue:** #259, #254
- **Decision:** the base-prompt variant uses the same `ImagePromptResult` schema. The second attempt, after a leaking draft, runs at the purpose's own temperature rather than at temperature 0.
  **Why:** at temperature 0 a regeneration from the same input would usually return the same text. The AC asks for one regeneration, not a deterministic one.
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** a draft with no appearance answers 422 at `definition.appearance` on both routes. The draft-base-prompt AC wrote `details.field: appearance`.
  **Why:** the same missing field gets one path everywhere, and every other catalog error names the document path (`definition.true_age`, `metadata.content_rating_id`).
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** authored ages are redacted (the planner's gate default) by `perceived.redact_ages`. It removes "N-year-old", "N years (old|of age)", "aged/age N", "N yo|y/o", their spelled-out forms (one to one hundred and ninety-nine), and the true age as a standalone number, then tidies the spacing and punctuation left behind. It applies to the appearance and to the base appearance prompt before either enters the view or the drafting call. A number that is no age ("Twenty-two freckles") is kept.
  **Why:** the gate default, and the AC's "never the age". The base appearance prompt is author text that enters the prompt too.
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** a scenario cover's scene is the cover constant followed by the public description ("establishing view of the setting; no people as subjects. <description>"). The Subjects section renders "(none)".
  **Why:** the planner's fixed sections leave the public description no section of its own. It describes the setting the cover depicts.
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** the add-on rule. A save refuses an add-on through `_validated` (`models.addon_errors`), at `body.visual_identity.adapter_params.addons[i].audience` with type `missing` or `enum`, beside the reference-image rule. A non-list `addons` and more than 10 are refused at `…addons`. A publish refuses a stored draft whose add-on is bad before the companion publish starts. That 422 is at `visual_identity.adapter_params.addons[i].audience`, with no `body.` prefix, because the publish body does not hold the draft.
  **Why:** the AC ("a save or publish … 422 validation_error"). The planner says stored versions are not rewritten, and a save can no longer store a bad add-on, so the race between the publish's unlocked read and its locked one cannot let one through.
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** the test names follow docs/04 IDs. The planned `test_draft_base_prompt` becomes `test_i_23__m8_draft_base_prompt` and `test_i_23__m8_catalog_prompt` keeps its name, both in `tests/integration/test_i_23.py`. `test_image_prompt_policy` becomes `test_c_22__m8_image_prompt_policy` in `tests/conformance/test_c_22.py`. `test_c_23__m8_visual_identity` and `test_addon_audience_required` (now `test_c_23__m8_addon_audience`) go in the new `tests/conformance/test_c_23.py`. `test_i_27__m8_style` goes in the new `tests/integration/test_i_27_m8.py`. The unit tests in `tests/test_prompt_builder.py`, including the `PerceivedView` structural test, carry no marker. I-27's story-image clause ("every image prompt for the story") is covered here by the scenario's cover prompt. #263's story variant adds story image prompts to the same file.
  **Why:** a part named with no docs/04 ID is unmappable, and there is one file per test ID and milestone. No story-image prompt exists before #263.
  **Issue:** #259, #263
- **Decision:** the registries. The FR-API-6 `/image-prompts` row is now `present` and leaves `PENDING`. The draft-base-prompt route is an `extras` row. Both routes are `route_flags(mutating=False)` and are named in `replay_support.UNKEYED_READS`. C-03 gains three steps: the latest version, a version the character lacks (404 on both surfaces), and the base-prompt draft. I-21 gains the draft-base-prompt `Call(200)`. `docs/openapi.json` is regenerated.
  **Why:** the replan's M3 #128 line.
  **Issue:** #259
- **Decision:** `ImagePromptUnavailable` (503 `image_prompt_unavailable`) joins `api/openapi.py`'s `ERROR_STATUS`. `build_image_prompt` and `draft_base_appearance_prompt` get `OPERATION_ERRORS` rows. A discovered C-01 flake, `GET /stories/{id}/operations` accepting an integer `until`, is filed as #788 (needs-triage, no milestone).
  **Why:** C-01 refused the undocumented 404 and 409 statuses. #788 is a route #259 does not touch.
  **Issue:** #259, #788
- **Decision (Rule 1):** CI run 42386620591 on `7d90e17` failed `test (rest)` on two tests. `test_library_strict_inputs` requires strict scalars in library input models, so `ImagePromptTarget.draft`/`.version` and `BaseAppearanceRequest.draft_revision` are now `StrictBool`/`StrictInt`. `test_strict_wire_schema_for_every_response_schema` (#761) asserted the emulation refuses "the last schema of the loop", which depends on set order: a schema bounded only by floats (`GuardrailVerdict`) or one with no wire form can come last, so it flaked. It now asserts the refusal on a fixed bounded schema (`ImagePromptResult`).
  **Why:** the strict-inputs rule is the library's. The #761 test's set-order dependence surfaced on this commit.
  **Issue:** #259, #761
- **Decision:** #260 step 0. Run 42386620591 on `7d90e17` had `test (rest)` red on two tests: `test_library_strict_inputs` (#259's `ImagePromptTarget.draft`/`version` not strict) and #761's `test_strict_wire_schema_for_every_response_schema` (its last assertion read whichever schema a set iterated last, and the emulation ignores float bounds). The #259 agent fixed both in `f24f3b1` while #260 ran; #260 made no fix of its own. The step-0 run is now 42388335919.
  **Why:** the orchestrator's heads-up. Two agents in one worktree: #260 staged only its own paths and regenerated `docs/openapi.json` from its final code.
  **Issue:** #259, #260, #761
- **Decision:** #260's store is `catalog.image_candidates` (migration `0135`, the planner's columns, plus `created_at` and an `asset_id` index), and `image_jobs.result` (jsonb, new column) holds a catalog job's `{candidate_ids}`. `asset_ids` keeps the real asset ids. `GET /image-jobs/{id}` keeps #256's top-level `candidate_ids`, read from `result`.
  **Why:** the planner's "candidate_ids in the job's result jsonb". A candidate row is deleted on attach or discard, so the ids must outlive it; storing candidate ids in `asset_ids` would make that column lie. A column is not a Rule 4 change.
  **Issue:** #260, #256
- **Decision:** `image_input_fingerprint` hashes `{content_rating_id, visual_style: {prompt, negative_prompt}}` plus, for a character, `appearance`, `true_age` and the whole `visual_identity`, through an in-module RFC 8785 serializer (`candidates.jcs`) over NFC-normalised strings. A character's style is `perceived.companion_style(conn, id, None)` (the companion's draft), the very function #259's builder reads. The draft always exists (a publish keeps it equal to the version), so the "no open draft" gate never applies: a request always builds from the draft at its current revision.
  **Why:** the planner's lines; one style function keeps prompt and fingerprint from disagreeing.
  **Issue:** #260, #259
- **Decision:** attach compares the candidate's fingerprint with the fingerprint of the draft as the save leaves it (after the patch), in the save's transaction after the revision compare and before `checked()`. A save that changes the appearance and attaches in one go is therefore `candidate_stale`. `{candidate_id}` refs are resolved to media ids before validation (`resolve`, unlocked) and checked again under `FOR UPDATE` (`attach`); `assert_referenceable` is unchanged and then sees a `live` asset. Character slots accept `ImageRef = Ulid | CandidateRef` (`extra="forbid"`); a scenario's `public_card` patch is free-form already. The import of `core.images.candidates` in `core.catalog.service` is local to the two functions, because of an import cycle through `core.catalog.models`.
  **Why:** the image is attached to the draft as saved; the planner's lock order and precedence.
  **Issue:** #260, #103
- **Decision:** the pipeline gains `jobs.TargetGone` and an optional target hook `revalidate(conn, job)` (read by `getattr`, so existing test targets need no change). It runs at claim and before each provider call; `TargetGone` there, or from `promote` (which rolls the promotion back), ends the job `target_gone` with the attempt `discarded` and staging deleted. Blobs copied to their keys before a refused promotion are left to the media sweep's orphan step, as #256 documents.
  **Why:** the planner's "entry gone early" line, without changing the `ImageTarget` protocol #263 implements.
  **Issue:** #260, #256, #263
- **Decision:** the catalog target registers itself on import (`orchestrator.images.targets.catalog`, imported by the Engine). Its `target` is `{entry_kind, entry_id, slot, content_rating_id}`. A candidate's asset uses the current version of the rating the request was built under (else Everyone's), and depicts `{kind: catalog_character, id}` for a character and nothing for a cover.
  **Why:** a candidate asset needs a rating version (NOT NULL) and promotion must not fail when the draft's rating changed meanwhile; the depicted subject lets #266 find it.
  **Issue:** #260, #266
- **Decision:** the local-store candidate URL is the existing signed `GET /media/{asset_id}/content`: `open_content` serves a `candidate` asset when the request's signature verifies (`signed`) or when the candidate content route asks (`candidate=True`), and marks it `private`, so both routes send `Cache-Control: private, no-store`. A credentialed read without a signature stays 404. `signed_url(candidate=True)` signs a candidate. `api.routes.media.content_response` is the shared 200/206/304 answer.
  **Why:** invariant 4 / ADR-152, the replan's Option A; one Range handler.
  **Issue:** #260, #107
- **Decision:** settings `candidate_ttl` (seconds, default 604800, 3600–7776000, whole hours, refused otherwise) and `catalog_candidates_n` (default 4, 1–10) join `ImageJobSettings` and `SettingsPatch`. `catalog_candidates_n`'s bounds are provisional: #262 owns the limits.
  **Why:** the AC names `catalog_candidates_n` as a deployment setting, and no story before #262 created it.
  **Issue:** #260, #262
- **Decision:** library methods `request_catalog_images`, `list_image_candidates`, `get_image_candidate_content`, `get_image_candidate_url` and `discard_image_candidate` each take `character_id=` or `scenario_id=` (exactly one), so `gate_catalog_methods` gates them, with routes `<method>_character`/`<method>_scenario`. The request is keyed (`request_catalog_images_<kind>` codecs, 202 `{job_id, status, config_revision, idempotency_key}`, `Location`); the discard is `route_flags(mutating=False)`, unkeyed and in `UNKEYED_WRITES`, like the job cancel. Entry deletes collect the candidates' bytes after commit (`Engine._collect`, checksums read before the delete, companions included); erasure's catalog delete removes the rows and leaves bytes to the orphan step.
  **Why:** the replan's naming; a keyed deployment mutation needs `config_revision` (`response_base_problems`).
  **Issue:** #260
- **Decision:** the tests follow docs/04 IDs. `test_i_25__m8_candidates`, `_candidate_expiry`, `_candidate_target_gone` and `_candidate_discard` (planned `test_candidate_discard`) are in `tests/integration/test_i_25.py`; `test_i_23__m8_candidate_metadata`; `test_x_07__m8_candidate_ttl`; `test_c_22__m8_candidate_no_checker` also covers the planned `test_candidate_not_configured` (adapter null → 409, no job). docs/04 §15's FR-IMG-7 row gains `I-25 (M8), C-22 (M8)`, which `check-traceability` required. Each test's outputs use a size of their own, so no two tests share a checksum on the shared database. C-03 gains the steps (both kinds' requests succeed with a registered PNG adapter); I-21's candidate routes expect 409 (no adapter), 200, 404 and 204 for owner and stranger alike.
  **Why:** a part named with no docs/04 ID is unmappable, and the plan's parts name FR-IMG-7.
  **Issue:** #260
- **Decision:** #261 step 0. The branch head was `9c03ff0` (#260), its CI run 42392470948 was green, and the worktree was clean.
  **Why:** the brief's precondition.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** `story_images` is registered as a derived table with `operation_id` as its only operation column. `deleted_operation_id` is not one. Visibility is `active_only(story_images)` and (no deletion, or the deletion's operation is not `active`), in `core.images.story_images.visible`. That deviates from the planner's "extra operation column `deleted_operation_id`".
  **Why:** a flip moves the rows of every operation column it names. Truncating a slot deletion would then discard the image instead of bringing it back. The planner's own visibility rule ("a deletion follows its own operation's membership") needs the deletion read through its operation, not flipped with it.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** `story_images.asset_id` has no foreign key to `media_assets`. The reference source (`public.story_images.asset_id`, plus a `REFERENCE_HOLDERS` row naming the story) keeps the asset alive. `deleted_operation_id` has a foreign key to `operations`. The CHECKs cover the position shape, the camera kinds (a character camera names `character_id`, no other kind does), the audience form, `source` and `viewpoint_basis`. `media_assets.viewpoint_basis` is nullable, with its own CHECK. Migration `0136_story_images` also adds `story_image` to the `operation_kind` enum.
  **Why:** the media sweep and erasure delete asset rows by their own rules (#266 owns erasure); a hard foreign key would make them fail on a referencing row. Other derived tables keep soft references the same way.
  **Issue:** #261, #266
- **Decision:** a `story_image_added` payload is `{image_id, asset_id}` and a `story_image_deleted` payload is `{image_id}`, both `narrative_state`. The event row's own `beat` and `slot_k` carry the position.
  **Why:** a slot's `k` is fixed only by its commit, after the payload is validated. The planner asks for ids and positions only, and the row has the position.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** a valid beat is any beat number the turn's active variant recorded (1 to its highest beat, the reply included). The planner's "a beat index ≥ the beat count" was read as "a beat the variant does not have".
  **Why:** taken literally, with the player input as beat 1, the rule would forbid the last beat (a Lite turn's reply). The demo places an image after a character's beat, and a reply is that.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** the upload stages the bytes and claims the idempotency key first, then runs the 422 checks (`position_invalid` → `viewpoint_invalid` → `camera_pov_invalid` → `camera_pov_not_present` → `subjects_required`), then #258's check and the moderation hook (`media.prepare`). Then one operation stores the asset (`media.commit(..., viewpoint_basis="none", record_control=False)`) and the row in a commit step. That step re-checks the position under the story lock: a changed active variant, or a moved last completed turn, is 422 `position_invalid`.
  **Why:** the request hash needs the bytes' SHA-256, so a replay answers the stored 201 even after the timeline moved. No check of a byte (#258) runs before the 422 checks, and staged bytes are not stored bytes. `media.commit` gained the two keywords so the asset is written in the story operation, not in a separate deployment `control` operation.
  **Issue:** #261, #258
- **Decision:** a `camera_pov_not_present` check passes only the audience's character to `present_at` as its actor, and then tests whether the camera's character is present. A camera character outside the cast is never present.
  **Why:** with the camera's own character as an actor, #541's rule makes it present trivially, and the check could never fail.
  **Issue:** #261, #257
- **Decision:** the library carries images beside the beats: `History.images` and `RespondResult.images`, each a list of `StoryImageItem`, with `History.sequence()` for the in-place order. The REST `items` and `beats` are `list[ItemModel | StoryImageItem]`, merged by `story_images.merge_into_history`. Respond's list holds the images within the returned turn's variant (always empty in #261, because an upload needs a committed turn; it matters for #263 and #265). The Lite, structured and staged result builders all fill it.
  **Why:** widening `History.items` to a union would retype every consumer of a beat's `text` and `channel`, tests included, under strict mypy. The REST shape the AC asks for is the same either way.
  **Issue:** #261, #263, #265
- **Decision:** `as_of=N` on a corrected read leaves out the slot images after N. The default read (no `as_of`) includes the head turn's slots.
  **Why:** the planner's #65 rule. If the default read left them out, every slot upload after the last completed turn would be invisible.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** the upload's 201 body is the omniscient item plus `operation_id`, `depicted_subjects`, `audience_viewpoint`, `timeline_revision` and `warnings`. `audience_viewpoint` is answered only there: history and the single read return images for their own viewpoint.
  **Why:** the AC (the omniscient item plus `operation_id` and `depicted_subjects`). C-24's "separate fields" check reads the audience back from the answer.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** a story without a rating needs the request's `content_rating_id` (422 `validation_error` otherwise). A looser rating answers `warnings: [{code: rating_looser, media_id}]`, using the guardrail-set comparison (`is_looser`'s rule, effective live guardrails).
  **Why:** the planner's FR-RATE-5 line. A story normally has a rating, so the 422 is a guard, not a path.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** the registries. `story_images` joins `STORY_TABLES` (after `scheduled_events`), `PRUNABLE_TABLES`, `SUBJECT_WRITERS` (`records.read_story_images` / `story_image_record`: the prompt as text, and as declared subjects the audience's character, the camera's character and the asset's depicted subjects) and `CONTENT_WRITE_PATHS` (`OPERATION`). The fork overrides map `audience_viewpoint` through the fork's id map and set `deleted_operation_id` to the fork's copy, or null. Bundles export the rows generically, `_media` adds their assets (deleted rows' included), `MEDIA_FIELDS` and the import carry `viewpoint_basis`, and the import's id map remaps `asset_id`.
  **Why:** the AC's References and Pruning, bundles, as-recorded lines. A fork that kept the source's deletion id would hide the image in a fork that did not copy the deletion.
  **Issue:** #261, #266
- **Decision:** the as-recorded read lists the omniscient images whose `story_image_added` is among the checkpoint's events and whose `story_image_deleted` is not (`History.images`, placed in `items` by REST).
  **Why:** owner decision 2026-11-06 and FR-STORE-23. The checkpoint's event set already applies the boundary and the membership as of then.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** the API registries. The FR-API-6 rows `POST /stories/{story_id}/images` and `DELETE …/images/{image_id}` are `present` at the served path templates, `GET …/images/{image_id}` is an `extras` row, and `PENDING` is empty. `test_c_15__api_surface` now asserts that no row is left `not_yet`; it used to expect exactly M8's. C-03 gains five steps: an upload, one with no subjects (422), a read, a delete and a read after it (404). I-21's `CALLS` get the three routes. The upload is `Call(422)`, because the matrix sends JSON and the route reads multipart. The read and the delete run on an image the owner uploaded. The error codes join `ERROR_STATUS` and `OPERATION_ERRORS`, `StoryImageUpload` is a `MULTIPART_BODIES` component, and `docs/openapi.json` is regenerated.
  **Why:** the replan's M3 #128 line and I-21 line. #263 extends the same POST for generation requests, so it needs no `PENDING` row.
  **Issue:** #261, #263
- **Decision:** the test names. `test_i_23__m8_story_images` and `test_i_23__m8_story_image_anchoring` (the planned `test_story_image_anchoring`, `part("M8", "FR-IMG-5")`) are in `tests/integration/test_i_23.py`. `test_c_24__m8_viewpoint_fields` is in `tests/conformance/test_c_24.py`. `test_story_image_upload_subjects`, `test_story_image_idempotent` and an added `test_story_image_refusal_order` carry no marker and are in `tests/integration/test_story_images.py`. The helpers are in `tests/story_image_support.py`. C-24's absent-camera case uses #257's rooms (`with_rooms`), because under Lite every character is present. S-DELETE plants a `story_images` row, and its foreign-key allowlist gains `deleted_operation_id → operations`.
  **Why:** a part whose name maps to no docs/04 ID is unmappable, and the traceability gate takes one file per test ID and milestone (#254's precedent).
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision (Rule 1):** the upload route calls `Engine.check_expected_revision` (erasure-gated, so it also refuses an importing or erasure-blocked story) before it reads the multipart body. `GET …/images/{image_id}` documents 403 `omniscient_required` for `include_audit`.
  **Why:** `test_i_10__m7_importing__running` requires every story route to answer 409 `story_importing` for an importing story, and the body's 422 came first. C-01 found the undocumented 403.
  **Issue:** #261

- **Decision (Rule 3):** CI run 42402401693 on `38142c8` failed `test (rest)` on two registries the local run missed. `story_images` joins `testing.determinism.ORDER`, ordered by position, then audience, camera and the asset's checksum. The operations reads in `core.images.story_images` filter through `active_operation` instead of a raw `membership` comparison (`check-membership`'s gate test).
  **Why:** neither `test_determinism` nor `test_membership_gate` was among the touched-area tests. CI's sharded run is the gate that catches them (#256's precedent).
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision (Rule 1):** #262 step 0. CI run 42403908312 on `8f25567` (#261's last commit) failed `test (integration-i-z)` in `test_i_08__round_trip`. Migration 0136 adds the `operation_kind` label `story_image`, which a downgrade cannot remove, and `KEPT_ON_DOWNGRADE` did not list it. Fixed in its own commit, `d970a71` (`Refs #261`).
  **Why:** the brief asked for #261's CI to be checked first and fixed under #261 if it was red because of #261.
  **Issue:** #261
- **Decision:** `insert_image_job` calls `core.images.limits.reserve` directly, after the job row and before the `jobs` row. It does not go through `PRE_COMMIT_HOOKS`, which stays as an empty seam. `store.insert_job` and `store.next_attempt` no longer write the attempt's row: `reserve` inserts it, `held`, with its accounting. Every new attempt (crash resume, retryable adapter error, check retry) goes through `ImageJobRunner._next_attempt`, which reserves inside a SAVEPOINT. On a refusal it rolls back to the savepoint and ends the job `cap_reached` in the same transaction (`_end_in`, split out of `end_job`). `status_reason` is `image_limit_reached` or `images_disabled`, and the new column `image_jobs.status_detail` is `{scope, period}`. The job read returns it only for `cap_reached`.
  **Why:** the record has immutable columns, so it cannot be written as `prepared` and then reserved by a later hook. A direct call keeps reservation and job in one statement order that is visible in one place.
  **Issue:** #262
- **Decision:** the attempt rows #256's code left without accounting are settled as follows, until #267 and #268 replace them. A return settles the attempt in the commit that records `returned` (`m` = every output the provider returned). An adapter error releases it. A crash-resumed attempt that was `sending` or `accepted` is settled as presumed (`used = requested`, `basis = presumed`), and one still `prepared` is released. A return whose record an ending already released (a cancel during the call) is not settled: it is logged with ids only and left to #267's late-return path. Every ending (`end_job`, `cancel_job`, promotion) calls `release_all`.
  **Why:** FR-IMG-11 says limits err toward generating less. Until #268's horizon exists, presuming the provider generated is the conservative choice, and #268's one-time correction can lower it later.
  **Issue:** #262, #267, #268
- **Decision:** every returned output is staged under its provider index. The first `n` are checked. Those at index `n` and beyond are deleted after the settlement commits, unchecked. A crash-resumed check reads only indexes below `n`.
  **Why:** the planner's pass-2 line ("all m outputs are written … those with k ≥ n are deleted in that commit's after-commit hook").
  **Issue:** #262
- **Decision:** the limit settings are fields of `ImageJobSettings` beside `catalog_candidates_n`. No time-zone setting existed (M6 has none), so `deployment_time_zone` is new there. The cross-check `catalog_candidates_n ≤ a non-zero image_limit_entry_day` is a model validator, 422 `validation_error` at `body` from either side. `apply_settings` checks the time zone before validating and answers 422 `invalid_time_zone`. Aliases are accepted (`US/Eastern`), and so is `UTC`. #260's provisional bounds for `catalog_candidates_n` (1 to 10) are confirmed.
  **Why:** the planner's bounds and gate default. A single section keeps the cross-field rule next to both fields.
  **Issue:** #262, #260
- **Decision:** the immutability trigger lets `story_id` change only to NULL, and only while `epistrel.allow_story_delete` names that story (the setting a story deletion already sets). Every other change to `job_id`, `attempt_token`, `requested`, `counter_keys`, `story_id`, `entry_kind`, `entry_id` or `created_at` raises `image_reservation_immutable`. `image_reservations` joins `STORY_ID_EXCEPTIONS`, `bundles.NEVER` and `determinism.OPERATIONAL_TABLES`. `image_limit_counters` joins the subject index's `EXEMPT_TABLES`. A story's deletion is also refused (423 `story_busy`, `job_running`) while one of its image jobs is `generating` or `checking`. Otherwise `release_for_story` releases what its jobs hold and nulls `story_id` before the jobs are deleted.
  **Why:** the AC makes `story_id` immutable, and decision 13 nulls it on deletion. The setting reconciles the two without a general escape hatch.
  **Issue:** #262
- **Decision:** the drift metric is `epistrel_image_counter_drift_total{scope}` (the project's `epistrel_` prefix). The reconcile job's `jobs.result` holds counts only, `{status, rows, drifted, stuck_held}`, and `/health` reads `checks.image_counters` from the latest `done` `image_counter_reconcile` job. `epistrel images reconcile` prints the report as JSON and exits 1 on drift. `--fix` releases stuck records (`release(touch=False)`), rewrites drifted sums, and writes an `image_counters_reconciled` audit row (actor `cli:images-reconcile`, `{stuck_held, deployment, entry}` counts), a new audit kind added in migration 0137.
  **Why:** the planner's reconciler lines. Ids and keys go to the logs only.
  **Issue:** #262
- **Decision:** retention treats a period as past `image_accounting_retention_days` when it is before today − N, in the current zone. A record's period is its first counter key's (an unreserved record's is its `created_at` local date). Records that are not `held` go first, and then counters that no record names any more, 1000 per batch.
  **Why:** the planner's retention line. A period closes at its next local midnight, and N days later it may go.
  **Issue:** #262
- **Decision:** the planned `test_reconciler_detects_drift` is `test_i_26__m8_reconciler_drift`. The planned stress run (200 jobs, 3 stories, 2 entries, concurrency 32, 60 s) is a part of its own, `test_i_26__m8_stress`, also FR-IMG-11. Every I-26 and C-24 limits test runs on a scratch database (`tests/image_limits_support.space`), and `IMAGE_TABLES_CLEANUP` deletes `image_limit_counters` too.
  **Why:** a bare test name maps to no docs/04 ID (#256's precedent). Limits and counters are deployment-wide, so a test changing them on the shared database would interfere with every other image test.
  **Issue:** #262
- **Decision:** the spec amendment also covers docs/04 I-23's "per-story caps reject excess requests" clause, and it adds a Limits paragraph to `docs/OPERATIONS.md` § Images. The ADR is ADR-181. It amends ADR-098 (per-story caps) and ADR-135 (the per-turn and per-story defaults), now partly superseded, with the inline markers and both indexes updated. `tzdata>=2026.5` is a runtime dependency, and `check-licenses` passes.
  **Why:** I-23 stated the removed rule too, and an operator needs the limits, the refusal codes and the reconcile CLI in one place.
  **Issue:** #262

- **Decision (Rule 3):** CI run 42409424556 on `ab0a90b` failed `test (integration-a-h)` in `test_health_db`, whose exact `/health` body lacked the new `checks.image_counters` (null with no database). Added there. `tests/test_health.py` had the same gap, and the local batch caught it before the push.
  **Why:** `test_health_db` was not among the touched-area tests.
  **Issue:** #262

- **Decision:** #263's perception reads are a new Core module, `core/images/story_perceived.py` (plain data: `story_perceived_inputs`, `StoryPerceived`/`StoryCharacter`, `viewpoint_matcher`, `UnperceivedIndex`, `style_and_guidance`), not added to `perceived.py`. The builder's story half is in `prompt_builder.py` (`story_view`, `build_story_image_inputs`, `write_story_image_prompt`, `story_parameters`, `consumer_prompt`, `FRAMING`, `REWRITE_INSTRUCTION`). The target is `orchestrator/images/targets/story.py`, registered on import by the Engine.
  **Why:** `perceived.py` is the catalog's allow-list (671 lines), and the story's reads (history, scene, identity, partitions, the protected index) share nothing with it but `perceivable_addons` and `redact_ages`. The import contract `images-generation-path-has-no-ages` still holds: `prompt_builder` imports `story_perceived` only, and ages become bands in Core.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** the filtered beats are `core.history.filtered_turn_beats` for the audience viewpoint over the anchor turn's active variant, cut at the position (a slot: the whole turn), `think` dropped. A turn is Lite when its operation recorded no `beat_*` event. Then the beats are the input and, past beat 1, the delivered message as the player saw it. A structured turn's assembled `message_rendered` is dropped, because it restates the beats. Beat lines are "<name> says: …" or "<name>: …", and an envelope keeps its own sentence.
  **Why:** the history read is #177's audience filter as consumers see it, so an image is never built from more than a history read for that viewpoint returns. Whether a turn is Lite cannot depend on what the viewpoint perceived: the guard, who perceived nothing, made a structured turn look like a Lite one.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision (Rule 1):** identity. `same_as` between two story characters is refused (`identity_merge_not_yet`, #171), so the masked stranger is a person entity paired with Marcus's character. A present character that is one side of a canon `same_as` with a non-character entity whose pairing the viewpoint does not hold is unrecognised. It is described by that entity's name ("the masked stranger"), also in the beat lines, and gets no appearance, visual identity, seed or references. Otherwise a character contributes its own catalog snapshot (`character_snapshots.content`: `definition.appearance` and `visual_identity`). `omniscient` and perception `none` recognise everyone. A non-player character holds a pairing by a canon fact its viewpoint reads or by its own belief, and the player only by a canon fact.
  **Why:** the planner's "identity only if the viewpoint holds `same_as`", which the data model can express only this way. Story characters have no visual identity of their own, only the catalog version they were made from. A story character's definition text is canon, and it carries secrets ("Jenni's lover"), so it never reaches an image prompt.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** cast and location. The cast is routing's co-located set (`perception.co_located_set`) at the viewpoint's own location, after the moves of the beats through the position, or everyone when nobody is placed. `omniscient` and perception `none` use the scene's location, which is the player's. Under Lite the cast is the characters the turn's texts name, plus the viewpoint. Labels are opaque (`person N`). A character viewpoint's location is the place it holds it is in (its own `located_at` belief, else a canon fact its viewpoint reads), by name only, and is omitted when it holds none. `omniscient` and perception `none` add the scenario's description of that location (`world.locations[].description`).
  **Why:** the planner's cast, location and "names never enter the prompt" lines. The scenario's description is canon and can name a concealed feature, so a character viewpoint never gets it. The guard behind the curtain is not co-located, so he is absent for Bobby.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** ages. A character viewpoint's own `age` belief about a subject wins: a number becomes its #170 band, and a decade without a third becomes "mid". Otherwise the band is #170's band of the current true age with its third made "mid". `omniscient`, perception `none` and the viewpoint's own band are exact.
  **Why:** the user's round-two band rule and the planner's pass-2 age fallback. A story character has no catalog apparent-age field, so the fallback starts from #170's band.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision (Rule 1):** the unperceived-beat index refuses on one shared 4-word shingle, or on a whole 2-3 word phrase. It does not reuse `match_thoughts`, whose hit needs two shingles or a 6-word run. The index covers every active turn's beats that the viewpoint did not receive at content: the omniscient read of the turn less its own read, so envelopes, partial eavesdrops, other characters' `think` and `latent`, and later turns are all included. Shingles of what the viewpoint did perceive are subtracted.
  **Why:** the AC says "a consumer prompt carrying a 4-gram of Jenni's whisper is refused". `match_thoughts` would let one 4-gram through.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** the prompt sections. `ImagePromptInputs` gains `beats`, `location`, `camera` and `instruction`, and `ImagePromptSubject` gains `label`. `image_prompt.j2` renders Location, What the viewer perceived and Framing only for a story image. It renders Instruction only on a rewrite. `docs/models.md` is regenerated. A built story prompt gets the style (as before) and then an `Image guidance:` section when it lacks the guidance. A consumer prompt is its text, then `Visual style:`, then `Image guidance:`, and its negative prompt is the style's.
  **Why:** the planner's "story sections as optional fields of the one template". The AC asserts the guidance is in the adapter request of a built prompt too, and a stub model's answer never contains it. Catalog payloads render as before.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** the request. `Engine.request_story_image` (REST: the JSON body of `POST /stories/{id}/images`, which dispatches on `Content-Type`) refuses in this order: the revision gate, `require_writable` (404 and 409 `story_archived`/`story_paused`), then `require_generation` (409 `not_configured`, then `image_check_unconfigured`), then `subjects_required`/`subjects_not_allowed`, then `place_at`'s checks under `body.` (`position_invalid` … `camera_pov_not_present`, the camera also having to be perceived by the viewpoint), then `viewpoint_perceived_nothing`, then the protected match on the caption and alt text (and a consumer's prompt), then the built prompt with one rewrite, then `prepare_image_job` (#257's check), then reserve and insert in one transaction. Schema errors (`extra = forbid`) are 422 `validation_error` at parse time, before the Engine. Any other content type keeps #261's 422 rather than a new 415. The answer is `StoryImageQueued` (202 `{job_id, status, timeline_revision}`, `Location: /image-jobs/{id}`), under codec `request_story_image` (story-scoped key).
  **Why:** the AC's and the planner's refusal order. FastAPI's usual body validation also runs first. A 415 would need a new code for a case #261 already answers.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision (Rule 1):** caption and alt text use the upload's limits (`media.CAPTION_MAX` 2000, `ALT_TEXT_MAX` 500), not the planner's 500 and 1000. Consumer prompts are 1-4000 characters, as planned.
  **Why:** the two bodies sit on one route and fill the same asset columns. An alt text the upload path would refuse should not get in through generation.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** the job. The target is `{story_id, audience_viewpoint, camera_pov, content_rating_id}`. The origin is `{story_id, operation_id (a ULID minted before prepare), turn, variant, position (the five columns the safety path reads), viewpoint, timeline_revision, request_position}`. `PreparedImageJob.extra_params` (new) puts `source`, `viewpoint_basis`, the final `depicted_subjects` and `references_dropped` into `image_jobs.params`. `promote` copies them verbatim. It inserts the `live` asset (`insert_output_asset` and `insert_generated_asset` gain `viewpoint_basis`), then `story_images.place_generated` (new): `Operation.begin_in`/`write_in` inside the promotion's transaction, under the job's `operation_id`, anchored as an upload's (`_operation` gains `operation_id` and `provenance`). `revalidate` only checks that the story exists. A `position_invalid` at promotion ends the job `target_gone`, as an interim until #264's `stale`. The job's `result` is `{asset_ids, image_ids}`.
  **Why:** the planner's job, origin and promote lines. #264 owns the rest of revalidation.
  **Issue:** #263, #264
- **Decision:** the safety path's viewpoint. `safety_checks.safety_request` strips `character:` from the job's viewpoint, so the audience character is an actor of #541's presence rule. Before, the full viewpoint string was compared with character ids and never matched.
  **Why:** a story job's viewpoint is stored in its output form (`character:<id>`), as the column documents.
  **Issue:** #263, #257
- **Decision:** `IMAGE_VIEWPOINT_GUARANTEE` lives in `core/media/checks.py` beside #258's statements. It appears verbatim in the route's description, the `images` tag's description and `docs/OPERATIONS.md` § Images (a new "Story images (FR-IMG-8)" paragraph). `test_i_24__m8_viewpoint_inputs` checks all three.
  **Why:** the planner's one-constant line.
  **Issue:** #263
- **Decision:** tests and registries. The AC's tests are named for docs/04 IDs: `test_i_24__m8_viewpoint_inputs` and `test_i_24__m8_masked_stranger` (I-24); `test_i_23__m8_story_generation`, `…_story_stored_prompt`, `…_story_guidance` and `…_story_camera_pov` (I-23); `test_c_22__m8_story_no_checker` (FR-IMG-3, C-22); `test_c_24__m8_consumer_prompt` (FR-IMG-9,10, C-24); `test_i_27__m8_story_style` (I-27). Unit tests are in `tests/test_story_perceived.py`, and the helpers in `tests/story_image_generation_support.py`. C-03 gains two `request_story_image` steps (202, and 422 `subjects_not_allowed`) and a `SHARED_ROUTES` entry, because the operation has no route of its own: `upload_story_image` serves both bodies. I-21's JSON call on `POST …/images` is now 409 `not_configured`. The FR-API-6 row is #261's.
