  **Why:** the test plan's names and files. The traceability gate maps a non-ID test name to its own §15 entry.
  **Issue:** #272, #773
- **Decision:** the discovered problem is filed as #794 (needs-triage, no milestone). `test_c_01[POST /stories/{story_id}/prune]` fails locally, and also on a clean 7c6e955 checkout: `TwoStageRequest` accepts `ignoreWarnings: 0`. It is not fixed here.
  **Why:** the problem predates #272 (`core/profiles/impact.py`) and lies outside its AC. CI was green on 7c6e955, so it does not block M8.
  **Issue:** #272, #794

## Ad-hoc — 2026-11-07 (#761: Anthropic structured calls go strict) — reconciled by /n8-replan 2026-11-09 (M9)

- **Change:** #761 shipped the owner's option 2 instead of the planned `strict: false`. Structured calls to api.anthropic.com now send `json_schema.strict: true` with a wire schema that has its bounds stripped (`provider_schema`). They get constrained decoding where they used to probe once and then fall back to parse-validate-retry. `DirectiveParseResult` (free-form `qualifiers` dict) stays on parse-validate-retry there. Every other endpoint's request is unchanged. The request shape is not a fingerprint input.
  **Why:** api.anthropic.com refuses a `json_schema` unless it is `strict: true`, and under strict it refuses bounds keywords. Found live 2026-11-07, decided by the owner on #761.

## /n8-exec M8 fix pass — 2026-11-08

- **Decision (method):** the fix pass covers the bugs `/n8-verify M8` filed against 920dba7 (#795–#801), on `milestone/m8-images-fixes` off origin/main 920dba7, one worktree agent per issue in sequence. Each agent runs its own tests, its area's test files and every static, gate and `--check` tool locally. CI's 12-shard run on the draft PR is the full-suite gate. #798 goes first because it bumps `current_milestone` to 8, so every later push is gated at M8.
  **Why:** a local serial full run takes over an hour; same practice as the M6 and M7 fix passes.
  **Issue:** #795–#801
- **Decision:** #798's three absent parts are marked on the existing tests that already assert each planned clause; docs/04 §15 is not amended, because its plan is right. FR-IMG-10 I-24 ("the checker's verdict is recorded per policy (FR-IMG-10)") → `test_i_24__m8_checker_true_ages`, which asserts the promoted asset's per-policy `(policy_id, result, certified)`. FR-MODEL-13 I-24 (the "Safety-call payloads (FR-IMG-13, FR-MODEL-13)" clause: registry schemas declare the inputs, the generated guide's rows list exactly them, with the retention note) → `test_i_24__m8_data_flow_rows`, which compares the guide's rows with `field_categories` of each safety purpose's input schema and the committed guide with `model_guide.render()`. FR-SCN-2 I-23 (the visual style in every image prompt and in no text prompt) → `test_i_23__m8_story_guidance`, which asserts both halves. No new assertion was needed. `current_milestone` goes to 8 in the same commit.
  **Why:** the bug's "Fix needs" (mark the test that asserts it, or amend the plan if it is wrong). Each test already asserts its clause as docs/04 states it, so new tests would only duplicate them. Cost if wrong: a clause is asserted more weakly than planned; each is named in its docstring for review.
  **Issue:** #798
- **Decision:** #797 narrows the type and extends the contract. The adapter's `ImageRequest` is built only in the new `orchestrator.images.request`: `build_image_request(RequestInputs, seed, params)` for a fresh attempt and `resend_request(snapshot, RequestInputs)` for a #268 re-send. `RequestInputs` (frozen: prompt, negative prompt, size, aspect ratio, quality, n, reference image ids) has no `safety_context`, and `jobs.py` narrows the `ImageJob` to it (`_request_inputs`); `_image_request` is gone. The `images-generation-path-has-no-ages` contract gains `orchestrator.images.request` as a source and `core.images.store` and `orchestrator.images.jobs` (the modules that hold an `ImageJob`) as forbidden. No existing source imports either, and TYPE_CHECKING imports count, so the builder cannot even name `ImageJob`. `tests/gates/test_image_paths_contract.py` adds a structural walk of the builders' signatures (no type of a forbidden module, no field or parameter whose `_`-word is `safety`/`age`/`ages`), an AST scan that nothing else in `src/epistrel` constructs an `ImageRequest`, and the contract bite on the request builder, each with a committed complement.
  **Why:** the bug's "Fix needs" and #257 AC 5 (the builder accepts only a value with no handle to canonical ages, under the contract). Forbidding the store module, not only `ImageJob` by name, is what makes the import contract bite: with 920dba7's contract a request builder importing `ImageJob` stays KEPT. The scan is what keeps a future builder from reappearing in `jobs.py`, outside the contract.
  **Issue:** #797, #257
- **Decision (Rule 1):** #795 deletes a slot image the way a beat image is deleted. `story_images.delete` records `story_image_deleted` in a `story_image` operation anchored at the image's own turn N (turn N's active variant, no slot). It no longer opens a new inter-turn slot after the story's current last turn. For a slot after genesis (`N = 0`) there is no turn to anchor to, so the deletion is position-less, as genesis records are. A chain (variant) read counts an active position-less deletion as on every chain. The deletion now holds through regenerate, swap, truncate and untruncate of later turns. It goes dormant or discarded only with turn N itself, and the image goes with it. A truncate to `N` or to a slot boundary before `N⁺k` discards the image and keeps the deletion, so an untruncate restores the image still deleted. A fork or bundle that copies the image also copies its deletion. Membership tracking stays: no new column, no new operation kind, no migration, no I-08 change, no change to invariant 6. The other option was a delete that is not membership-tracked, which would have made a slot delete behave differently from a beat delete. Deletions recorded before this fix keep their old slot anchoring; there is no backfill. #261's Table AC sentence ("An upload or deletion … at an inter-turn slot it is a new slot operation") is superseded for deletion only; uploads are unchanged.
  **Why:** the bug's "Fix needs" (a deletion anchored where it holds whichever later turns are kept) and the brief's choice: match beat-image deletes, which anchor at the image's turn and stay deleted. Turn N is the earliest anchor that no operation can retire without also retiring the image. Inserting the deletion into the image's own slot `N⁺k` would need `Operation` to position into an existing slot, which owner decision 14 rules out ("never inserts a slot into the past"). Cost if wrong: the deletion's own event sits at turn N, ahead of its image's `N⁺k` in log order. Nothing orders replay by that position; rows carry the deletion by id.
  **Issue:** #795, #261
- **Decision:** #796 makes `limits.retain` follow #262's Retention AC as written. A closed-period record that is settled or released is deleted only when no `held` record names any counter in its `counter_keys`: a correlated `NOT EXISTS` over `jsonb_array_elements(counter_keys)` against the `held` records' `counter_keys @>`. The counter pass is unchanged (a counter goes only when no record names it), and the return shape stays `{records, counters, costs}`. The rule applies to released siblings too, so `test_i_26__m8_day_boundary`'s old step "the released record goes, the held one and its counter stay" now keeps the released record until the held one ends. Every record names its period's deployment counter, so one held record keeps its whole day's records. That is what keeps every kept counter equal to its kept records. `costs.purge` (#269) is unchanged: #269's planner note sets it by `period_date` with no state condition, cost rows are not in the counters' sums or the reconciler, and a late return whose cost row was purged already inserts a `late_unaccounted` row.
  **Why:** the bug's "Fix needs" and #262's Retention AC ("every record naming them is settled or released"). Deleting a settled sibling left its `used` on the kept counter, so the reconciler reported false drift and `reconcile --fix` would have lowered `used`. Keeping a released sibling (which adds 0) is not needed for correctness, but it matches the AC literally and keeps one rule. Cost if wrong: released rows of a day with a long-held record stay until that record ends, a few rows per day.
  **Issue:** #796, #262, #269
- **Decision:** #799's eight complements go into the tests the issue names, or else the story's own `test_<id>__m8_*` test, with no product code changed. #256 goes into `test_i_25__m8_crash_sweeps`. #258 goes into `test_c_22__m8_output`. #259 and #261 go into `test_i_23__m8_catalog_prompt` and `test_i_23__m8_story_images`. #263 goes into `test_i_24__m8_viewpoint_inputs`. #266 goes into `test_c_24__m8_subjects`. #268 goes into the `presumed_then_actual` group of `test_i_26__m8_ambiguous`. #265 gets two new I-23 parts (`part("M8", "FR-IMG-6")`): `test_i_23__m8_auto_unconfigured` (lifted from the verify probe) and `test_i_23__m8_auto_staged_abandoned`. Each guard was mutated locally, the new assertion was seen to fail, and the guard was restored. The evidence is on #799. No test found wrong behaviour, so there was no Rule 1 fix and no issue to file.
  **Why:** the issue's "Done when" (each box has a committed test that fails when its guard is removed). The two #265 cases need their own setup (a story with no adapter configured, and a staged turn held by its provider), so they are new tests rather than branches of an existing one.
  **Issue:** #799, #256, #258, #259, #261, #263, #265, #266, #268
- **Decision:** two #799 items are asserted below the REST surface, because the API cannot reach them.
  - **#266, the own-image attach.** After a catalog-scope erasure the character's draft is gone, so an attach is 404 first. While an erasure is pending, the catalog gate answers 503 first. The test therefore calls `core.images.subjects.include_own` directly for the erased character, which raises 409 `erased_subject_referenced` at `body.depicted_subjects`. That is the transaction a draft write racing the erasure would run.
  - **#268, "losing its target".** A run whose attempt is ambiguous returns `waiting_for_horizon` before it revalidates its target, so a target loss shows up only as an ending. The test ends the job with `end_job(…, target_gone)`, the call every target-gone path makes.
  - **Also noted:** the #266 issue text says a non-erased consumer prompt "returns 201". Generation queues a job, so it returns 202, and that is what the test asserts. In #256, `staged_files()`'s skip of the `images` name duplicates its files-only filter. What keeps `tmp/images/` safe is that the scan does not recurse, so the bite mutates the scan into a recursive one.
  **Why:** each item's guard is asserted where it can be reached. A REST-only test of these two cases would pass no matter what the guard does. Cost if wrong: a future REST path to either case would be covered only at the library level.
  **Issue:** #799, #266, #268, #256
- **Decision:** #263's orphaned `orchestrator.images.prompt_builder.build_story_image_inputs` is removed, with its `__all__` entry and the two imports only it used (`Placement`, `story_perceived_inputs`). Nothing in `src`, `tests` or `docs` called it. Production is not routed through it: `targets/story.perceived_view` needs the raw `StoryPerceived` for its two refusals (`camera_pov_not_present`, `viewpoint_perceived_nothing`) before it calls `story_view`, so a wrapper that returns only the `PerceivedView` cannot be its seam.

Each new assertion was seen to fail under a mutation of the branch it covers, and the evidence is on #800. No test found wrong behaviour, so there was no Rule 1 fix and no issue to file.
  **Why:** #800's checklist. Cost if wrong: none to behaviour, because these are tests only.
  **Issue:** #800, #258, #260, #263, #264, #265, #266, #267, #268, #272
- **Decision:** three of #800's tests reach their branch through a seam, not through REST alone.
  - **#264.** The erasure cancels a depicting job in its own transaction (#266), so `revalidate`'s `Stale("erased")` is the last line of defence. The test makes `store.cancel_in` a no-op. Mutating that branch away lets the erased subject's image be attached (`promoted`), so the branch is load-bearing.
  - **#272.** The import exclusion in `_recorded_image_results` is not the complement: an import re-checks its images with the configured checker and stores those verdicts as the story's. Instead, the complement is an image uploaded before any checker was configured (no recorded results), which is asked about both policies.
  - **#265.** A staged auto turn's in-request completion is made to fail (`staged.write_report`). Then each of `staged.resume`, `staged.resume_stalled` and the `outbox_recovery` handler (`outbox._recover`) completes one such turn and queues its job.
  - **#266.** A truncation leaves its rows `discarded` only until the next turn, which shelves them `dormant`. So the test truncates last, after the regeneration that makes the other image `dormant`.
  **Why:** a REST-only test of these cases passes whatever the branch does, or cannot reach it. Cost if wrong: these branches are covered below the REST surface.
  **Issue:** #800, #264, #265, #266, #272
- **Decision (Rule 1):** #801's `n` item: `plan_body` clamps `n` to the smallest `n.max` the chosen endpoints list (`Endpoint.n_max`, read from `supported_parameters.n.max`; `Route.n_max()`), in one call. Clamped to 1 it is not sent and is recorded under `dropped_parameters`, as an unlisted `n` already was. Clamped to k > 1 it is sent as k, not recorded dropped; `requested.n` and `sent.n` show the difference. The request is not split into several calls.
  **Why:** #255's planner note ("`n` unlisted → sent as 1 and recorded dropped (one call; the job settles the outputs it got)"): a clamp is the same rule with a bound, and fewer outputs than `n` is already a partial success. The smallest max is used because the serving endpoint is not known before the call. Before this, `n = 2` against the recorded model's `n: {max: 1}` was a non-retryable 400 (`ImageRequestInvalid`). Cost if wrong: fewer candidates than asked from a mixed-max route.
  **Issue:** #801, #255
- **Decision:** #801's `resolution` item: `resolution` leaves `CANONICAL_PARAMETERS` (stop advertising it), and the adapter's success log now names the dropped parameters (`dropped=`). No `ImageRequest` field, no config parameter and no size-to-resolution mapping is added, so a configured `size` on a model that lists only `resolution`/`aspect_ratio` is still dropped, and recorded so. The operator configures `default_aspect_ratio` for such a model. #255's Request AC text ("`aspect_ratio` or `size`/`resolution`") overstates what ships; its planner note "Size and ratio are not translated" holds.
  **Why:** the smallest correct fix. Carrying `resolution` needs a new request field and a new `image_generation` param (a public config contract change, Rule 4). Mapping `size` to `resolution` is the translation #255 ruled out, and the recorded model's values (`768`, `1K` … `4K`) do not map from `WxH` without a table per model. The constant was matched against nothing, so dropping it changes no request.
  **Issue:** #801, #255
- **Decision:** #801's dedupe item is documentation only. The recorder's dedupe check compares the generation `id` of two answers, and OpenRouter's image answers carry no `id` (all four recorded generations, 2026-11-08), so against OpenRouter it can only answer `dedupes: false, inconclusive: true`. That is noted in `tools/record_openrouter_fixtures.py`'s docs and on `OPENROUTER_DEDUPES_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`. The constant stays `False` and the `Idempotency-Key` header stays unsent. Turning it on needs other evidence of deduplication, for example two billed costs against one.
  **Why:** the brief (document, don't change behaviour). Cost if wrong: none; a repeated send is already handled as ambiguous by #268.
  **Issue:** #801, #255
- **Decision:** #801's #258 item: the `policies.on_uncertain` column deviation is accepted (the orchestrator's call; the owner can override). The output check keeps reading #49's `rule.on_uncertain` (`violation` → `block`, `pass` → `allow`), as the M8 entry above ("no `policies.on_uncertain` column") records. #258's Columns AC gains an amendment line pointing here. - **Decision (Rule 1):** #810 is fixed in `image_check.j2`, not in the seeded policy. The template now carries a framing line ahead of the policy list: each policy's text says what it forbids; texts written for text checks are applied to the image and its subjects; any answer format a policy's text asks for is ignored. The template's `verdicts` format is the only answer. Policy texts are listed verbatim, as before. The checker fingerprint moves with the template's SHA (FR-PROF-16), which is harmless: no image-check certification exists, because E-11 has not run. The seeded `PROMPT`, its policy version and `guardrail_check` are unchanged, so no migration is needed and no text-check certification goes stale.
  **Why:** I captured #271's real `image_check` requests with a local stub. They showed the minors policy's text-check prompt ("You are checking a text … Answer JSON {violation, confidence}") listed inside the image check, which asks for `{"verdicts": …}`. That conflict risks off-format answers, which turn into `uncertain`, which blocks under `on_uncertain: violation`, and the E-11 run would have certified that. A template fix also covers admin-authored policies that apply to both text and image targets; rewriting the seed would fix only the seed. Cost if wrong: a model may still lean on the policy's "text" framing. The E-11 run measures that.
  **Issue:** #810, #271

## #271 E-11 run — 2026-11-09

- **Decision (owner):** the E-11 checker is `claude-haiku-5-5`, hosted on api.anthropic.com through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, in place of a local vision model. The local `qwen/qwen3.8-27b` took about 12.5 s a check (about 7.5 h for the run); Haiku took about 1.4 s, and the run finished in 6 minutes at `--concurrency 8`. A free `count_tokens` pass over 8 captured real requests measured about 1,754 input tokens per check, so the run costs about $0.50–1.50. Batch processing was ruled out for now: it would save under $1, and it needs the native Anthropic endpoint, which invariant 1 (OpenAI-compatible endpoints only) does not allow.
  **Why:** the owner's choice after the price lookup and the token count. #271's plan allows a hosted run (owner 2026-11-06).
  **Issue:** #271
- **Decision (owner):** the E-11 set is relabelled: implied nudity is `clean` under "The image shows no nudity". The first run (`no_nudity` FN 17.8%) prompted a review of every `no_nudity` violation image, grouped by how often the checker flagged it. 46 cases went to `clean` (none of them shows nudity), and `no_nudity-adversarial:cropped-0012` was dropped as a malformed image. That leaves `no_nudity` with 105 violation and 198 clean cases, and the set with 719. The owner re-approved the set on 2026-11-09. The first run's report was measured against the old labels and was not committed. The floors were not touched.
  **Why:** the first review had labelled implied nudity as a violation. A label must say what the image shows.
  **Issue:** #271
- **Decision (owner):** the run's result is accepted as it stands. `minors_no_sexual_content` passes FP (0.00%; FN is not measured; certified only by external attestation). `no_nudity` fails its FP floor: FN 0.00%, but FP 9.76% ± 0.77% against 10%, because Haiku flags implied nudity. `no_nudity` stays an uncertified backstop for this checker, and no certification record is earned. The owner judged a slightly conservative checker acceptable. More model and prompt testing comes later, including a policy wording that says whether implied nudity is allowed.
  **Why:** #271's AC asks for the committed report, not a pass. Lowering a floor after seeing the result was ruled out.
  **Issue:** #271

  - A present benched character is visible to the others and its actions may be narrated, but it never speaks.

  - all-benched turns still run;

  - present characters' actions may be narrated, never voiced;

  **Issue:** #828
- **Decision (Rule 1):** I-10's `test_create_refuses_bad_requests` "cast size" case now sends 201 characters (over `STORY_CAST_LIMIT_MAX`, refused at `body` with `cast_max`), not 21. This was a fourth CI fix push for #828, one past the brief's three. Each push fixed a different failure, every one caused by #828 (capability map, traceability row count, C-16, I-10). This one was a one-line test expectation, verified locally (I-10: 36 passed), so I pushed it rather than leave the branch red for the next story.
  **Why:** run 42830741913's integration-i-z shard failed. The M2 test still expected the old 20-character cap.
  **Issue:** #828
- **Decision:** #824's store and validation live in Core (`core/purposes/`: `validation.py`, `output.py`, `store.py`; tables `consumer_purposes` and `consumer_purpose_versions`, migration `0145`), and resolution in the Orchestrator (`orchestrator/models/consumer.py`). The built-in names a consumer purpose may not take (every delivered and reserved purpose, every port, `default`) come from `consumer.builtin_names()`, which the Engine passes to `store.register` as `reserved`.
  **Why:** the architecture rule keeps Core from importing the Orchestrator, where the registry lives. The `Purposes` value the Engine passes to profile validation is the same pattern.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** the 100-live-purpose limit is checked inside `lock_deployment`'s transaction, not under a separate advisory lock as the planner line put it.
  **Why:** every consumer-purpose write already takes the deployment row `FOR UPDATE` (the configuration-write rule, #48), which serialises concurrent creations just as an advisory lock would. A second lock would add nothing.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** a consumer purpose's capability floor is `StructuredOutput.PARSE_VALIDATE_RETRY` ("structured output": constrained decoding, or output reliable enough to parse, validate and retry), the floor `guardrail_check` declares.
  **Why:** the AC says "the capability floor is structured output". `JSON_SCHEMA` would demand constrained decoding, which `structured_call` does not need, because it falls back to parse-validate-retry.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** in `/admin/model-config`, every field and param a consumer purpose does not set reads `source: inherited`, whatever `generation`'s own source is. `rating_suggestion` instead reads `default` when `guardrail_check` has no row. The `Sources` response model is unchanged; no `inherits_from` key was added.
  **Why:** the planner line says "`sources` shows `inherited: generation`". A consumer purpose uses `generation`'s effective value, so "inherited" is accurate even when `generation` takes it from `default`. Adding a key would change the response schema of every entry.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** `PUT`, `GET` and `DELETE /admin/model-config/{name}` answer 404 `not_found` (`details.reason: archived`) for an archived consumer purpose. An unknown name keeps its existing 422 `validation_error` (`reason: unknown`). The check runs under the deployment lock in `_store`, through `config.require_configurable`.
  **Why:** the planner line says "unknown or archived consumer name is 404", but an unknown name cannot be told apart from a mistyped built-in one, and the 422 for it is an existing M2 contract. Only the archived case is new, and it is 404 as planned.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** a `PUT /admin/purposes/{name}` identical to the latest version writes nothing and answers `changed: false` at the same version and `config_revision`. A repeat archive is 200 with `changed: false`.
  **Why:** "a write that changes nothing writes nothing" is the rule for model config, providers and profiles. The AC's "writes version n+1" holds for every replacement that changes something.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** each consumer-purpose write records one prospective `config_changes` row, `consumer_purpose:<name>`, whose values are `{version, sha256}` (and `{archived}` for an archive). It never records the template or schema text.
  **Why:** invariant 3's spirit. Consumer templates may carry consumer content, and the change log is listed over REST. The digest still shows that a version changed.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** the compiled output model names its fields `p0`, `p1`, … and gives each the schema's property name as its alias. `core.purposes.output.output_of(instance)` dumps a reply by alias. The schema subset also restricts property names to `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$` (`schema_invalid` otherwise).
  **Why:** aliases let any allowed property name work, including names that shadow `BaseModel` attributes (`json`, `model_config`). The planner was silent on property names; a bounded pattern keeps prompts and wire schemas sane.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** the AC's "a stub call (#825) goes to the overridden model" is proved at the Model Access Layer. `ModelAccessLayer.send(name, …)` under the stub records `call.model == "consumer-model"` after `PUT /admin/model-config/{name}`, and `generation`'s model again once the override is dropped (`test_i_29__m9_routing`). `send` now accepts a live consumer purpose (`ModelAccessLayer.check_purpose`) and refuses an archived one (410). #825 extends the same test with its REST call.
  **Why:** #825's call route does not exist yet. `send` is the seam that route will use, so the test exercises the routing #825 relies on.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** `ContentCategory.CONSUMER_INPUT` is the consumer purpose's only input category, and `never_receives` is every other one. The viewpoint category is left to #826. `docs/models.md` is regenerated: it gains the category's description and no purpose rows.
  **Why:** the planner line names "consumer input and viewpoint". The viewpoint context's shape is #826's to define, and a category with nothing tagged by it would be dead.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** engine profiles and story overrides already refuse a consumer purpose name in `models.purposes` with 422 ("is not a model purpose" at `body.settings.models.purposes.<name>`), because `Engine.purposes` lists only registry purposes. No code changed; `test_i_29__m9_never_a_turn_purpose` proves it.
  **Why:** the AC is met by the existing check. A consumer-specific message would need a database read inside a synchronous validator.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision (Rule 3):** `api/openapi.py`'s `STATUS_TEXT` gains `410: "Gone; nothing was written"`.
  **Why:** `replace_purpose` is the first operation to declare a 410 (`purpose_archived`). `export_expired`'s 410 was never declared on an operation, so `openapi --write` raised `KeyError: 410`.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** I-29 is a new docs/04 integration test ID, "Consumer purposes". Its M9 parts are in `tests/integration/test_i_29_m9.py`, and C-02 gains an M9 part (`test_c_02__m9_purposes`). FR-MODEL-14's §15 row names both. `tests/gates/test_traceability.py` now expects 442 §15 rows, and docs/04's per-milestone count line reads `M9 2`. ADR-185 is the next free number.
  **Why:** the conventions require it: one file per test ID and milestone, and the counts #828's notes say to bump.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision (Rule 3):** C-03's parity steps gain the six consumer-purpose operations: register, replace, get, versions, list, archive. They are placed before the provider steps, so `delete_external_provider` stays the last step, which `test_c_03_bites_on_a_method_without_a_route_or_step` relies on. `PurposeReplace` gains an OpenAPI example (C-01's raw-body example check).
  **Why:** C-15's surface and replay checks and C-01's example check failed locally without them. They require every Engine operation to have a REST and library parity step and every body to have an example.
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision (Rule 3):** `PurposeReplace.expected_version` is typed `StrictInt`, and two docstrings in `core/purposes/validation.py` say "no whitespace" where they said "compact".
  **Why:** CI run 42862656994's `test (rest)` shard failed two checks. `test_library_strict_inputs` requires every library input integer to be strict (#427), and `test_no_compaction_term` bans the word (ADR-175).
  **Issue:** #824
- **Decision:** #825's call module is `orchestrator/purposes/call.py`, built as separate steps: `check_inputs`, `prepare` (resolve, rating, guard context; takes an extra `cast` for #826), `render` (takes `viewpoint` and `story`, `None` here), `gate_inputs`, `generate` and `gate_output` inside `produce` (the one output retry, then fail closed), and `assemble`. The model call goes through a new `structured.structured_messages`: the constrained-decoding and parse-validate-retry loop of `structured_call`, factored out so it takes messages already rendered. `structured_call` now calls it after its deterministic step, unchanged in behaviour.
  **Why:** the key link names `ModelAccessLayer.structured_call`, but that path renders through `prepare` and `get_delivered`, which refuse consumer names; a consumer purpose's messages come from its own templates. Factoring the loop keeps one structured path (json_schema mode, probes, retries) and `send`'s model-config routing for both.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** the call's response also carries `config_revision` (the deployment revision its configuration was read at) and the echoed `idempotency_key`, beside the AC's `{purpose, version, output, model, usage}`.
  **Why:** `POST /purposes/{name}/calls` is a mutating route (it honours `Idempotency-Key`), and `responses.response_base_problems` requires every deployment-scoped mutating response to extend `DeploymentMutationResponse`.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** `Engine.call_purpose(ctx, name, inputs, *, version, content_rating, depicted, deadline_ms)` takes the idempotency key from `ctx`, as every other Engine method does, not as an `idempotency_key` keyword as the planner line wrote it. `content_rating` is a rating id. `deadline_ms` has a minimum of 1. An unknown purpose name (a built-in one included) is 404 `not_found` (`PurposeNotFound`), mapped from the resolver's 422 `UnknownPurpose`.
  **Why:** the request context is the library's idempotency convention (`_keyed`), and ratings are referenced by id everywhere else (`content_rating_id`). The AC asks for 404 for an unknown purpose; the 422 stays for `send` and `/admin/model-config`, which #824 kept.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** migration `0146_purpose_output_audit` adds the `audit_log` kind `guardrail_output_rejected`, so the output refusal can write its row with no story. `EntryPoint.PURPOSE_CALL` (`purpose_call`) is new. The output row's details are the entry point, the purpose's name and version and the attempts; never text.
  **Why:** the planner line names the row. A turn's rejected output is a story event, so no audit kind existed for it, and `ck_audit_log_kind` refuses an unlisted kind. A new CHECK value is not a new table.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision (Rule 2):** model metrics, the `model_call` span and the Model Access Layer's log lines (`access.py`, `errors.map_provider_error`, `openai_compatible`) label a consumer purpose `purpose="consumer"` (`metrics.purpose_label`); the call log keeps the real name for `usage`.
  **Why:** the planner line says metrics never carry the name, and `record` labelled every call by its purpose name. Logs got the same label, so no operator-chosen name reaches an operational log either.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision (Rule 1):** the stub's `conformant_example` answers a schema field by its alias and dumps by alias.
  **Why:** a consumer purpose's output model names its fields `p0`… aliased to the property names, and validates by alias only, so the stub's default answer raised a validation error instead of answering. A schema without aliases is unchanged.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** the output gate checks each deterministic output policy against each string leaf on its own, and each model-assisted policy against the leaves joined into one text, each line labelled `output.<path>: <text>`. Each gate's model-assisted checks run on a budget of exactly G calls under the call's deadline, as `input_budget` sizes the other gates. The purpose's own budget is 2 × (1 + `structured_retry_budget`). The deadline is re-checked before the output gate, so an unchecked output past it is a 503, never a fallback verdict.
  **Why:** "keys are not gated": a wordlist matched against the labelled text would hit a key name in a label. The model-assisted check needs the labels for context, as the planner line says.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** `model.version` in the answer is the latest version the model reported (FR-PROF-16, `reported_version.latest`), or `null`. Epistrel's fixed preamble is the rating's prompt guidance under `## Content rating guidance` (when it has any), then a `## Task` instruction to answer with only the schema's JSON object; the purpose's `system_template` follows it in the same system message.
  **Why:** the planner gives `model = {endpoint, model, version}` without saying which version; the purpose's version is already top-level. #824's `system_template` field description promises this preamble.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** #825's tests are new slices of I-29 ("Consumer purposes") in `tests/integration/test_i_29_m9.py`, marked `part("M9", "FR-MODEL-15")`: `test_i_29__m9_call`, `_call_refusals`, `_call_input_gate`, `_call_output_gate` and `_call_library`. `test_i_29__m9_routing` (still FR-MODEL-14) gains the REST call to a second stub endpoint. FR-MODEL-15 joins docs/03 (§13 and the §22 `M9` row), its §15 row names I-29 (M9), the traceability check expects 443 rows and the count line reads `M9 3`. `tests/policy_support.rated_policy_rating` takes extra policy fields (`applies_to`).
  **Why:** one file per test ID and milestone; I-29 already covers consumer purposes, so a new I-30 would split one capability over two IDs.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision (Rule 3):** the operator-path enumeration (`api/routes/admin.OPERATOR_PATH_PATTERNS`) no longer lists `purposes` as a plain segment: a path naming `purposes` is an operator path unless it ends in `purposes/{name}/calls`, so the consumer call route (and #826's story-bound one) is not "misplaced" outside `/admin`. `inputs` is typed `dict[str, Any]` with a JSON-values validator, not pydantic's `JsonValue`, and a new OpenAPI tag `purposes` files the call route.
  **Why:** C-02 and C-15 failed locally with `/purposes/{name}/calls` reported as an operator path outside `/admin`; C-01 refused the `JsonValue` component (no title or description) and an untagged operation.
  **Issue:** #825
- **Decision:** #826's story-bound call is `orchestrator/purposes/story.py` (`read_story` prechecks, `prepare_story`, `refuse_erased`, `build_viewpoint`, `story_of`, `call_story_purpose`), reusing #825's `call.gate_inputs`, `call.render`, `call.produce` and `call.assemble`. `PreparedCall` gains `actor` (the viewpoint character, for character-scoped input policies) and `render_ids` (the character-scoped output policies that apply: the viewpoint's, or none; `None` keeps #825's story-less behaviour), and `PurposeResult` gains `timeline_revision` (`None` with no story). The REST answer `StoryPurposeCallBody` extends `MutationResponse` (`timeline_revision`, the story's as the call read it) and also carries `config_revision`. The Engine method is `call_story_purpose(ctx, story_id, name, inputs, *, version, viewpoint_character_id, deadline_ms)`, keyed per story as `story_purpose_call:<name>` (codec `call_story_purpose`).
  **Why:** the planner names the library method; `responses.response_base_problems` requires a story-scoped mutating route to extend `MutationResponse`. Reusing #825's steps keeps one safety path.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** the order inside a story-bound call is: the prechecks (404 story, 409 `story_archived`, 404 character, 422 `player_has_no_context`, 409 `module_off`), the purpose's resolution, the rating and guard context, the erased-subject check, the input gate, then the viewpoint (embedding calls), then the render, then the output. A template that does not render is therefore refused after the input gate here, not before it as in #825.
  **Why:** the AC says a violating input is refused with zero model calls. The viewpoint's retrieval embeds the query, which is a model call, so the gate has to come before it, and the render needs the viewpoint.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** the character render's knowledge sections move into two shared partials, `viewpoint_self.j2` (the definition, the deflection style, the age, the beliefs, the sense of time, the private memories) and `viewpoint_scene.j2` (the scene, working memory, just now, retrieved, canon). `structured_generation.j2` includes them where the sections were, and the new `viewpoint.j2` includes both. The render's prompt is byte-identical: 43 renders of `example_instance(GenerationInputs)` (full, each optional field emptied in turn, and all emptied) were compared before and after.
  **Why:** the render keeps its pinned memories and rolling summary between the two halves, and moving them would change the prompt every eval and golden test sees. Two partials keep one text for both paths without reordering the render.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision (Rule 1):** `orchestrator/models/facts.TEMPLATE_HASHES` hashes each story purpose's template followed by every template it includes, depth first, each once (`template_source`). `tests/test_profile_facts.py` follows. This moves the fingerprint of every template that includes another (`structured_generation`, and those including `steps_contract.j2`/`clock_contract.j2`), and `evals index` is regenerated.
  **Why:** with the knowledge sections in partials, editing one would otherwise leave the render's fingerprint unchanged, which breaks FR-PROF-16's "prompt-template versions". The same gap already existed for the contract includes.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** `build_context(conn, character_id, state, *, query=None, lazy=True)` takes the call's joined string inputs as `query` (in place of the perceived input) and `lazy=False` to skip `_needed`. These are keyword arguments, not `TurnState` fields. The call builds the `TurnState` at `next_turn_index` with the latest committed scene (`scene_view` at the head, omniscient), no pending beats, the deployment's real embedder and lexical ports and no adjudicator, inside one `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` transaction.
  **Why:** these are the planner's "optional `query`" and "lazy resolution off". As keyword arguments the turn's calls stay unchanged.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision (Rule 1):** a story-bound call never touches the memories its retrieval returned (`last_accessed_at`). `build_viewpoint` runs inside `retrieval.pipeline.deferring_touches()` and never flushes it.
  **Why:** the first run failed with `cannot execute UPDATE in a read-only transaction`, because retrieval touches every memory it returns. The AC says a call never changes the story, and a call is not a turn that used those memories.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** the template's `story` is `{id, title}` for every call without a viewpoint, on a Lite story, a shared-knowledge story or a partitioned one. With a viewpoint it adds `location`, `present` (names, sorted) and `scene`, which is the viewpoint's own `## Scene` line (`CharacterContext.scene`, with apparent ages).
  **Why:** the planner gives id and title for a partitioned story without a viewpoint, and is silent on the other stories without one. The narrower shape is never wrong, so it applies everywhere. The viewpoint's scene line is the scene text a render of that character shows.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** a story-bound call's guard context is `policies.store.guard_context(story)` with no actors, so a cast member counts as present when co-located at the latest scene's location. Its rating is the story's (`story_guidance`), whose guidance leads the preamble. The player's character as the viewpoint is 422 `validation_error` with `details.reason: player_has_no_context` at `body.viewpoint_character_id` (as `build_context`'s refusal is), and a viewpoint on a Lite story is 409 `module_off` with `module: pipeline`.
  **Why:** these are the planner's guardrail and error lines. No dedicated error class exists for `player_has_no_context`; `build_context` already raises it as `InvalidRequest` with that reason.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** an input naming a subject erased from the story is checked with `erasure.guard.check_content` as consumer text with no base revision, so every story-scope erasure of the story counts: 409 `erased_subject_referenced`, before the input gate. `call_story_purpose` also declares `config_key_missing` (503), which the guard raises without a configuration key.
  **Why:** the planner says such an input is 409 "as on other inputs". The guard exempts consumer text only when the operation's base revision is at or after the erasure. A call reads the head and has no operation, so it has no base revision to exempt it.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** `tools/gates/character_context.py` covers the purpose path. `viewpoint_inputs` must take a `CharacterContext` first, and may pass `ViewpointInputs` only context sections plus `character_definitions` (`VIEWPOINT_SECTIONS`), never a turn-shaped one (`VIEWPOINT_OMITS`: `player_input`, `just_now`, `tracked_values`, `tracked_syntax`). A `Viewpoint(...)` built outside `orchestrator/structured/viewpoint.py` is a finding. So is a `render_viewpoint(x)` whose `x` the same function did not assign from `viewpoint_inputs(...)`. `viewpoint.j2` and what it includes are scanned for narrator-only names. Three gate tests show each rule biting, and the repository passes.
  **Why:** the story's note says the gate must cover the purpose path (NFR-PRIV-4). The same AST rules that hold the render now hold the viewpoint.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** #826's tests are new I-29 M9 slices in `tests/integration/test_i_29_m9.py`, marked `part("M9", "FR-MODEL-16")`: `test_i_29__m9_story_viewpoint` (the isolation pair on the Sunday Dinner, Father against Mother, with the root word "letter"), `_story_refusals`, `_story_guardrails`, `_story_read_only` (a turn held in flight with `concurrency_support.start_turn`), `_story_routing`, `_story_library` and `_story_erased`. FR-MODEL-16 joins docs/03 (§13 and the §22 `M9` row), its §15 row names I-29 (M9), the traceability check expects 444 rows, the count line reads `M9 4`, and the capability map puts FR-MODEL-16 on the floor. The C-03 parity step `call_story_purpose` follows `call_purpose`. The FR-API-6 route row and an ownership `CALLS` entry are added (an unknown purpose, so 404 for anyone).
  **Why:** these are the conventions. One file per test ID and milestone, and I-29 covers consumer purposes.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** the complement (fail-first) was run. With `build_viewpoint`'s `TurnState` given the story's settings with `character_knowledge.partitions` false (a viewpoint built from the omniscient, unfiltered context), `test_i_29__m9_story_viewpoint` failed at `assert SECRET_ROOT not in …`, because the Father's prompt held "the love letters." The code was then restored and the test passes.
  **Why:** the test plan asks for the isolation test to fail against a deliberately wrong implementation before it is trusted.
  **Issue:** #826
- **Decision:** #827's write follows the inter-turn slot pattern `core.states.api.set_state` uses. `turn_slot(db, story, op_id)` takes the story's turn slot as a turn does: 423 `story_busy` under `reject`, or a wait under `queue`. `open_inter_turn(source=consumer, operation_id=op_id)` then sets `holds_turn_slot`, and the commit positions the slot at `N⁺k` after the head turn. It all lives in `orchestrator/purposes/story.store_memory`, called after `produce` (the model call stays unlocked) and before `assemble`. The commit step re-checks the modules and the character (`_character`: 404 if it is gone, the player refused) and reads its own `purpose_memory_stored` event id for `source_event_ids`. The memory id is minted before the event, because the event's payload names it.
  **Why:** "Locking: only the write takes the story lock (423 while a turn is in flight)". A turn holds no row lock during its model calls (FR-CONC-2), so only the turn slot can refuse while a turn is in flight. `set_state` is the existing consumer write in an inter-turn slot that does exactly this. `open_inter_turn`'s own docstring asks a slot to record a non-audit event so a fork copies it.
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** `purpose_memory_stored` is registered in category `derived`.
  **Why:** the planner line says "the memory category", but `EventCategory` has none (`narrative_state`, `input`, `derived`, `amendment`, `audit`, `control`). `consolidation_output`, the other event that records a memory write, is `derived`. A non-audit category is what makes a fork copy the slot.
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** the memory writer is the new `core.memory.records.write_purpose_memory` (not `write_episodic`). It writes `character_id` = the holder (the erasure index's `authored_by`) and `beat` NULL, and the slot operation's `narrative_turn`/`turn_variant` give its position. It runs `MEMORY_HOOKS` (embedding, importance) but not `EPISODIC_HOOKS` (consolidation's scheduler). The resurrection guard checks the text as non-consumer content (model output is never exempt) at the slot operation's base revision.
  **Why:** `write_episodic` writes one shared row per beat event, which is the wrong shape. `write_resolution`, a single private memory with holder and actor the same character, is the closest model. The planner names the embedding hooks and the importance job, and says nothing about consolidation. Compressing a one-character memory into consolidated memory is outside this story.
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** the text refusals are two new error codes, 422 `memory_text_empty` (`MemoryTextEmpty`) and 422 `memory_text_too_long` (`MemoryTextTooLong`, `details.limit`/`actual`). `text_field_invalid` and the missing viewpoint are 422 `validation_error` reasons. The missing viewpoint's reason is `viewpoint_required`, at `body.viewpoint_character_id`, checked first (`check_store`).
  **Why:** the planner writes the two text refusals as codes and `text_field_invalid` as "422 with reason", and names no reason for the missing viewpoint. `call_story_purpose` declares the new codes plus `story_paused` and `story_busy` (`revision_conflict` is added for every story mutation already).
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** with `store_as_memory`, the call also checks `expected_revision` (`Engine.check_expected_revision`, a start-time precondition) and `require_writable` (409 `story_paused`) in its prechecks. It checks the modules there too, after #826's Lite 409: `partitions`, then `episodic`, each a 409 `module_off` naming its module, at `body.store_as_memory`. The write re-checks writability before it takes the turn slot. A read-only call is unchanged.
  **Why:** every story mutation starts with the expected-revision check (FR-RESP-6), and the planner says "re-check archived, paused" at write time. The module order follows the planner line "With episodic off and partitions on: 409".
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** migration `0147_consumer_purpose_provenance` adds `record_provenance` value `consumer_purpose` (autocommit `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE`, as 0129 does). Its downgrade leaves the value, so I-08's `KEPT_ON_DOWNGRADE` gains `("public.record_provenance", "consumer_purpose")`. `trust_tier_of` maps it to `in_world`.
  **Why:** the planner's enum migration. Postgres cannot drop an enum value.
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** FR-MODEL-17 joins docs/03 §13 and the §22 `M9` row. FR-MODEL-16's "Read-only" clause gains "(unless it stores its result as a memory, FR-MODEL-17)". The §15 row names I-29 (M9), the traceability check expects 445 rows, the count line reads `M9 5`, and the capability map puts FR-MODEL-17 on the floor. The FR-MODEL family is in no FR-PROF-13 clause, and the requirement's own refusal covers the stories it does not serve. The tests are new I-29 slices marked `part("M9", "FR-MODEL-17")`: `test_i_29__m9_memory_isolation`, `_memory_timeline`, `_memory_erasure`, `_memory_idempotent`, `_memory_refusals` and `_memory_library`. Their partitioned stories are `new_story` plus `PUT engine-profile` with `sp.partitioned_profile`.
  **Why:** these are the conventions, and #826's FR-MODEL-16 already sits on the floor the same way.
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** the viewpoint check for `store_as_memory` stays "a non-player character of this story" (`_character`), with no participation-role check.
  **Why:** #831 (benching) relies on storing a memory for a benched viewpoint, such as a juror's vote reason.
  **Issue:** #827
- **Decision:** a subject image's declared subject is stored in `depicted_subjects` as `{kind: "subject", id, label, true_age}` (a per-request ULID), but `subject` is **not** added to `core.tables.media.SubjectKind`. `MediaAsset.depicted_subjects` reads `DepictedSubject | SubjectDeclaration` (the new model takes `kind: Literal["subject"]` with the label and true age). `media_record` skips the `subject` kind when it indexes an asset (`INDEXED_SUBJECT_KINDS`), and `core.images.subjects._sorted` keeps each declaration whole. The safety path gets the declaration through `SafetyRequest.inline` (`InlineSubject`), not through `SubjectKind`.
  **Why:** the planner wrote "stored as `SubjectKind.SUBJECT`". That enum also drives the `subject_references.subject_kind` CHECK (`SUBJECT_KIND_CHECK`), the upload's `DepictedSubject` (consumers could then declare `subject` on any upload) and every erasure reader that rebuilds `SubjectKind(kind)`. No erasure can name a subject that exists nowhere in Epistrel. Keeping `subject` out of the enum gives the same stored shape with no widened CHECK and no new upload input. `_sorted` used to rebuild entries as `{kind, id}`, which would drop the label and true age once a catalog draft took a subject image (the read would then fail validation).
  **Issue:** #830
- **Decision:** the prompt check for a subject image also checks the consumer's own description and style. They become `SafetyRequest.consumer_texts`, scanned by the deterministic policies and joined to the model-assisted check text as "Subject description:" and "Style:" lines, beside the prompt `image_prompt` built from them.
  **Why:** the built prompt is a model's rewrite. A prompt writer that drops or softens what the consumer asked for would let a sexualizing description through a check of the rewrite alone. FR-IMG-3 checks "every image prompt — built by Epistrel or supplied by the consumer", and the description is the consumer's prompt in all but name. The planner says the style is "checked as part of the prompt"; the description gets the same treatment. FR-IMG-14 states it.
  **Issue:** #830
- **Decision:** two migrations. `0148_subject_image_jobs` widens `image_jobs`' kind (`subject`) and status (`completed`), adds `ck_image_jobs_completed_subject`, and widens `image_reservations`/`image_costs` `entry_kind` to `subject`. Its downgrade deletes subject jobs and their records. `0149_media_asset_origin` adds `media_assets.origin` (null or `subject`, CHECK `ck_media_assets_origin`). No enum type changes, so I-08's `KEPT_ON_DOWNGRADE` is unchanged.
  **Why:** these are the planner's job kind, status and `origin` column, one migration per table concern. They take the next numbers after `0147_consumer_purpose_provenance`.
  **Issue:** #830
- **Decision:** a subject job's `target` is `{subject_id, content_rating_id, content_rating_version_id}` (the rating's version at the request) and its `origin` is `{subject_id, label, true_age, description, style}`. Its reservations are attributed `entry_kind = subject` with the subject id and charge the deployment counter only (`limits.attribution`, `costs` late-unaccounted attribution). Promotion writes live assets owned by `job.principal`, and the job's `result` is `{asset_ids, failures}`. A failure's `reason` is `guardrail_violation` when that output's check failed in the promoted attempt, else `provider_empty_result`. `GET /image-jobs/{id}` adds `kind: subject` and `failures` (absent for other jobs). A job that ends `failed` reports no `failures`; its `policy_ids` say why.
  **Why:** these are the planner's accounting and result lines. The job's origin already carries the label and true age for the safety path, so the asset's declaration comes from it rather than from a second copy.
  **Issue:** #830
- **Decision:** the only mid-job revalidation (`SubjectTarget.revalidate`, and again inside `promote`) is "an offboarding of the job's principal, asked at or after the job's `created_at`, not `failed`, whose media action is not `keep`" → `TargetGone`, so the job ends `target_gone` with nothing stored.
  **Why:** the planner names offboarding as the only revalidation. A principal has no row that offboarding deletes, so the offboarding request is the signal. With `media: keep` the owner keeps its media, so the job completes. `transfer` also ends the job rather than handing new images to the receiver unasked.
  **Issue:** #830
- **Decision:** FR-IMG-14 joins docs/03 §18.7 and the §22 `M9` row. FR-MEDIA-2 gains the live-subject-image exemption with an *[amended by ADR-186]* marker. ADR-186 amends ADR-113 (its index row reads `Amended | 186`, and the FR-MEDIA and FR-IMG area rows gain 186). docs/04 gains I-30 (`tests/integration/test_i_30_m9.py`, slices `request`, `refusals`, `minor_refused`, `flagged_outputs`, `kept_and_reusable`, `offboarding`) with its §15 row. The traceability check expects 446 rows, the count line reads `M9 6`, and the capability map puts FR-IMG-14 on the floor. The offboarding slice runs on a scratch database (`migrated_database`), because it runs the job worker.
  **Why:** these are the conventions, and I-30 is the next free ID.
  **Issue:** #830
- **Decision:** `character_bench` (migration `0150_character_bench`, `core/tables/bench.py`) holds one **version** per bench state change, the `scheduled_events` pattern: `character_id`, `mode` (CHECK `sequestered`/`present`), `benched` (true for a bench, false for a reactivation), `previous_role`/`previous_fixed`, and the writing operation's position (derived columns plus `slot_k`/`beat`/`step`, CHECK turn non-null). A character's state at a position is its latest active version there (`core/bench.py`: `bench_states(conn, story, before_turn=None)`, `bench_of`, `absent_from_scene`). It is registered with `membership.register_derived`, joins `STORY_TABLES` (a fork copies it), `determinism.ORDER` and the bundle export by default, and is exempt from the subject index (ids, a mode, a role, positions; the events are indexed).
  **Why:** the planner's re-simulation line asks for a derived table (character id, mode, since position) that truncate, untruncate, swap and fork maintain. A single row per character cannot be un-reactivated by a truncation, because a row follows one operation's membership. Version rows can, with no special follower. #832 adds a mode switch as one more `benched` version in the new mode, valid from its own position, with no schema change.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** bench and reactivate take the story's turn slot (`states.api.turn_slot`) and open an `inter_turn` slot operation (`open_inter_turn`, `holds_turn_slot`), like `set_state` and #827's `store_memory`. They also check `_refuse_busy(turns_only=True)` before the operation and again in its commit step. The event and its refusals are decided before anything is written and re-decided under the story lock. Precedence: 404, then 409 `story_archived` (and a paused story's refusal), then 409 `revision_conflict`, then 423, then 422 (`player_not_benchable`, `unsupported_mode`, `cast_max`), then 409 `already_benched`/`not_benched`. The events are `character_benched {character_id, mode, previous_role, previous_fixed}` and `character_reactivated {character_id, mode, restored_role, restored_fixed}`, category `control`. Reactivation rewrites `characters.participation_role/fixed` from the bench version.
  **Why:** the planner names `_refuse_busy(turns_only=True)` as the 423. Holding the turn slot too keeps a turn from starting between the check and the commit, so the slot is positioned after the head turn the check saw. It also means a `queue` story waits rather than refusing, as every other inter-turn slot write does. The payloads name the character (the planner's `{mode, previous_role, previous_fixed}` has no subject), and `restored_fixed` mirrors `previous_fixed`.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** perception drops a `sequestered` character in one place, `core.epistemic.scene.load_scene`. It reads `bench.absent_from_scene(conn, story, turn)` (the versions before that turn) and leaves those characters out of the scene's cast, placements, channels, languages and consciousness. It also sets the new `SceneState.absent`, so `co_located` never lists them, `moved()` never places them, and `route_perception` drops them as perceivers whatever the beat's qualifiers say. Roles and rendering drop benched characters through `StoryCast.benched` and `StoryCast.active()`: `read_story_cast` reads the bench at the head, and `orchestrator.lite.cast.refuse_benched` refuses any request field naming one with 409 `character_benched`. It then answers the active cast to Lite and structured `respond` and `run_queued`, so default render selection, `roles.resolve` and the Lite author notes never see a benched character. A regenerate reads `turns.cast_at_turn` (the bench before that turn) and keeps its recorded ids. `core/epistemic/roles.py` and `exposure.py` themselves are unchanged.
  **Why:** the issue's key links name `route_turn`/`co_located_set` and `resolve_roles`. Every caller of those (turn routing, exposures, memories, audiences, image presence, preconditions, settlement) builds its scene with `load_scene`, and every caller of `resolve_roles` takes the turn's cast. Filtering at those two sources covers them all, and a new caller can't forget the bench. The fail-first run (the scene filter off) failed `_sequestered` with one exposure for Bobby and `_history` with Bobby holding turn 2's line.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** a character read's `bench` (`CharacterBody.bench`) is **omitted** while the character is not benched, as `role_id`, `source` and `participation` are. The bench and reactivate responses (`BenchedCharacterBody`) carry `character` (omniscient) and an explicit top-level `bench` that is `null` after a reactivation. `GET /stories/{id}` adds `cast {active, benched}`: `active` is `_active_cast_count`, and `benched` counts the cast's benched characters.
  **Why:** the planner says "`bench` on every `CharacterView`", and "200 returns `CharacterView` plus `bench` … or null". An always-present `bench: null` would change every exact character body the suite and the Console compare. Omitting it follows the body's own convention for optional fields, and the mutation responses still say `null` explicitly.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** `_cast_full` also refuses when benched and unbenched `major` characters together reach `STORY_CAST_LIMIT_MAX` (`cast_max` with `limit: 200`). This covers adding a character and a `minor`→`major` promotion. Reactivating a `major` character checks `_cast_full` (the active count against `max_story_cast`); a `minor` skips it. A respond request's 409 `character_benched` is decided before cast resolution and the archived check.
  **Why:** these are the planner's "total ceiling" and "minors" lines. The benched check runs first because an unknown-id 422 would otherwise hide that the id is a benched character.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** FR-MULTI-13 joins docs/03 §16 after FR-MULTI-12 and the §22 `M9` row, as one requirement with clauses for the routes, the refusals, the deliberate writes, the modes, Lite and the positional rule. It is on the floor (the capability map and FR-PROF-13's per-character clause say "FR-MULTI-12 and FR-MULTI-13 are floor"; `FLOOR_POINTERS` gains it). docs/04 gains I-31 (`tests/integration/test_i_31_m9.py`, slices `round_trip`, `refusals`, `cast_count`, `out_of_turns`, `sequestered`, `history`, `deliberate_writes`, `lite`, `library`) with its §15 row and the §14 overview. The traceability check expects 447 rows, and the count line reads `M9 7`. There is no ADR, per the planner.
  **Why:** these are the conventions. I-31 is the next free ID. Benching holds under Lite too, so it is a floor requirement, as FR-MULTI-12 is.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** S-PRUNE's table-coverage check failed on #831's CI run 42933746659 (C-08 runs S-PRUNE nested): `character_bench` carries an `operation_id` and was neither pruned nor retained. It joins `PRUNABLE_TABLES` after `scheduled_events`, so a pruned slot operation's bench versions go with it. Committed separately (1d13539, `Refs #831`). [Rule 1]
  **Why:** a discarded bench is a discarded derived record, like a discarded schedule; keeping it would leave rows pointing at a deleted operation.
  **Issue:** #831
- **Decision:** `present` joins `core.bench.SUPPORTED_MODES` and the 422 `unsupported_mode` path is removed (I-31's refusal test drops the assertion that pinned it until #832). The mode switch `PATCH /stories/{id}/characters/{cid}/bench` `{mode}` (`core.stories.set_bench_mode`, `Engine.set_bench_mode`, codec `set_bench_mode`) runs through #831's `_bench_change` (turn slot, `open_inter_turn`, the check repeated under the lock) and writes one more `benched` version in the new mode with the bench's `previous_role`/`previous_fixed` carried, so no migration. The event is `character_bench_mode_changed {character_id, mode, previous_mode}` (category `control`). The same mode is a 200 no-op decided before any operation opens (no event, the current timeline revision). There is no `If-Match` (the planner's line). Refusals: 404, 409 `story_archived`/paused, 423, 422 for an unknown mode (the body's `Literal`), 409 `not_benched`.
  **Why:** #831's version rows already carry a position per change, which is the planner's "valid-from position per mode row", so a switch is just another version and rewind, regenerate and fork treat it like the bench.
  **Issue:** #832
- **Decision:** one presence set for the scene read and the scene line: `core.projections.structured.scene_view` now drops a `sequestered` character's entity and marks a `present` one (`SceneView.bench` entity→mode and `benched_characters` entity→character, using the bench before turn `as_of + 1`, the same position `load_scene` uses for the next turn). `GET /stories/{id}/scene` lists it as `present[]` with `bench {mode: "present"}` (omitted otherwise; `PresentEntityBody`). The structured scene line, each character's `## Scene` (`context._scene_line` over `TurnState.present`) and #826's `story.present` all read it, so a present-benched character is named and a sequestered one is not. Perception itself needed no change: #831's `load_scene` already keeps a `present` bench (it is outside `ABSENT_MODES`), so exposures, beliefs, memories, audiences and the other `load_scene` consumers treat it as present. I did not audit each of those consumers one by one.
  **Why:** before this, the scene read came from placement facts and ignored the bench, so a `sequestered` character still appeared in every scene line. The AC needs the scene line to drop it and name a `present` one. Fail-first: with the filter off, I-32 `_visible` failed on "Present: Bobby (early twenties), Jenni, …" for a sequestered Bobby; with `present` added to `ABSENT_MODES`, `_perceives` and `_no_widening` failed (0 exposures).
  **Issue:** #832
- **Decision:** the prompt line "Present but not taking part: <names>; never give them dialogue." is one `{% if present_benched %}` block in `structured_generation.j2` and `narrator_generation.j2` (right after each "Your part" voice rule) and `lite_generation.j2` (after "Each character knows only…"). `GenerationInputs.present_benched` (`C.SCENE`), `RenderSections.present_benched` (set from `TurnRead.present_benched`, the scene's present-benched names, sorted), and the character-context gate classifies it `TURN`. Lite reads the bench as its turn starts (`bench_states(before_turn=…)`) and names every present-benched character, since Lite has no location. `evals index` was re-run. Rendering every template with the full and the sparse example inputs (with `present_benched` empty) gave byte-identical output before and after the edit.
  **Why:** these are the planner's lines. Lite's prompt has no `## Scene` section, so on Lite the prompt line is the mode's only effect. The planner named "the scene line and that one prompt line", but there is no scene line to change there.
  **Issue:** #832
- **Decision:** the verify exception is `core.verify.permission`'s "present-bench exception". A `director` or `character` asserter's claim is permitted with the new basis `bench_present` when its predicate is in `BENCH_PRESENT_PREDICATES = {holds, located_at, present_at}`, its subject is benched `present`, and every other modeled character it names is too. `PermissionFacts.bench_present` is read in `facts_for` from `bench_states` before the claim's turn. That read isn't keyed: a bench change holds the turn slot, so none can land mid-turn. Speech (`spoke`, `spoke_to`), backstory, a claim also naming an unbenched character, and any claim about a sequestered or unbenched character keep #144's denial. It is tested both ways in `test_i_32__m9_verify_exception`. No ADR: FR-MULTI-14's own text scopes it and FR-VERIFY-11 is unchanged.
  **Why:** the orchestrator asked for the narrowest exception. Non-speech observable actions map to those three predicates (the co-author set minus speech). A thought or a decision never becomes a claim about another character's beat.
  **Issue:** #832
- **Decision:** narration describing a present-benched character's action stays in the describing primary's beat with no code change. `roles.collect` passes `prose_reactions` only the turn's role-holders, and a benched character has none, so "Bobby shifts in his seat." is never split into a beat of Bobby's (`_visible` asserts the beat is Jenni's). `turn_report.bench {present: [ids]}` is written only when the turn saw a present-benched character, so existing exact turn reports don't change.
  **Why:** these are the planner's "actions in prose" and "reads and reporting" lines, implemented as the smallest change.
  **Issue:** #832
- **Decision:** FR-MULTI-14 joins docs/03 §16 after FR-MULTI-13 and the §22 `M9` row. It is on the floor: FR-PROF-13's clause now reads "benching, FR-MULTI-13,14, are floor", and `FLOOR_POINTERS`, the capability map and the `per_character_renders` comment follow. docs/04 gains I-32 (`tests/integration/test_i_32_m9.py`, slices `switch`, `cast_count`, `perceives`, `no_widening`, `visible`, `never_renders`, `verify_exception`, `lite`, `library`) with its §15 row and the §14 overview. The traceability check expects 448 rows and the count line reads `M9 8`. I-31's docs/04 line drops `unsupported_mode`. The ownership fixture `_benched_character` keeps a bench that is already in force, because the PATCH entry and the reactivate entry share the story's Ada.
  **Why:** these are the conventions. I-32 is the next free ID, and the mode holds under Lite in its prompt form, as FR-MULTI-13 does.
  **Issue:** #832
- **Decision:** P-11 runs in-process through REST on the stub, not as a `perf.lite_smoke` compose workload. `tests/perf/cast_support.py` builds each cast with the key room's recipe: Structured (M4) v1, partitions on, testimony `defaulted`, perception `co_location`, per-character renders. Participation is set at creation, fixed. The cast is the player plus 3 primaries plus N−4 silent (or reactive) characters, so "a 50-character story" holds 50 full characters, the player included, which is how `max_story_cast` counts them. The budget is `budgets.model_calls = 50`, the schema's ceiling; the planner said "raised", and 100 is refused.
  **Why:** these are the planner's lines (a pytest perf test under `tests/perf/`, `perf_weekly`, sequential, budget raised). The in-process run reuses the multi-character test helpers and the stub's call log that the complement needs. Engine-only time is the respond call's wall clock with the stub at 0 ms. Statements are counted with #620's probe (`write_turn_body` on the awaiting stack). Each primary render must happen exactly once per turn, and `stories.next_turn_index` must equal the turns played, or the run fails as failed, lost or reduced.
  **Issue:** #829
- **Decision:** `perf.yml` gains a `weekly-casts` job (Sunday 03:00 UTC with the others, and on dispatch with `suite: weekly` or the new `suite: casts`). It is separate from the 3-hour scale job, and `weekly-docs` doesn't wait on it. The committed figures come from dispatching `suite: casts` on the milestone branch (run 42945569537, GitHub-hosted runner, labelled "not the reference host"). The repo is public, so the run costs no owner spend and makes no live model call.
  **Why:** the planner's "the scenario runs in CI's perf job" and "figures come from the GitHub runner". The weekly job's pytest step names its files and its summary greps `p_0[126]`, so a job of its own keeps P-11 from colouring the gated scale suite. `perf_docs` is not extended, as the planner said, so the owner commits the artifact `perf-casts` by hand.

- **Decision:** the "Large casts" guidance is a README section placed right after "Configuration", the README's deployment-settings section. FR-MULTI-12's text in docs/03 now ends with a sentence citing it and P-11. No new FR, so the §15 row count stays at 448 and the count line at `M9 8`. FR-MULTI-12's §15 row gains `P-11 (M9)`, and the §14 overview gains "Performance P-11 §11".
  **Why:** the AC asks for the section "in the operator docs where deployment settings are described" and for FR-MULTI-12 to cite it. The planner puts it in README's deployment-settings area.
  **Issue:** #829
- **Decision:** the results are named `perf/results/2026-11-11-casts.{json,md}`, after the runner's UTC date (measured 2026-11-11T02:25:32Z), not 2026-11-10. The P-11 statement growth (about one per co-located character) is a once-per-character `characters.is_player` read in the commit (#619's memoised `partitions.is_player`; probed at 10 and 30 characters, +20 reads and +1 other statement). It is reported, not changed: lowering the cost is out of scope (#754, M11, covers commit batching).

## /n8-exec M9 fix pass — 2026-11-10

- **Decision:** the fix pass runs on `milestone/m9-verify-fixes` in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/m9fix`, off `origin/main` at 522cd68. The four stories are small, so they ran in this session, not one background agent each. Each was checked locally with ruff, format, mypy, lint-imports and the touched modules' tests (702 passed); the full-suite gate is CI's sharded run on the PR, as in the M9 run.
  **Why:** the main checkout holds the owner's `m8-e11-evidence` branch and uncommitted `.idea` edits, which the run must not touch.
  **Issue:** M9 (#14)
- **Decision (Rule 1):** a consumer template's item keys must be constants (a slice is allowed). `inputs['_' ~ '_class__']` and `inputs[inputs.k]` are refused at save, not only those whose computed key happens to start with `_`.
  **Why:** FR-MODEL-14 refuses "an item whose name starts with `_`" at save, never at call time. A computed key's name is unknowable at save, so the requirement can only hold if computed keys are refused.
  **Issue:** #837
- **Decision (Rule 1):** the `attr` filter is refused outright. The other built-in filters that read attributes by a name (`map`, `selectattr`, `rejectattr`, `sort`, `groupby`, `sum`, `unique`, `min`, `max`) need a constant name with no `_`-prefixed dotted or comma-separated segment, and no `*args`/`**kwargs`.
  **Why:** #837 named `attr` only, but `map(attribute='__class__')` reads the same attribute by the same route. The rule is the requirement's "reads an attribute whose name starts with `_`", wherever the name is written.
  **Issue:** #837
- **Decision (Rule 1):** the consumer-template environment has no Jinja globals, so `range`, `cycler`, `lipsum`, `dict`, `joiner` and `namespace` are refused at save as undeclared variables, and render as undefined.
  **Why:** FR-MODEL-14 allows only the top-level variables `inputs`, `viewpoint` and `story`. Clearing the globals keeps the check and the renderer in step through one environment.
  **Issue:** #837
- **Decision:** #838, #839 and #840 are test-only. Product behaviour was already correct (the verification probes), so each issue closes with the complement test that guards it. #837, #838 and #839 share one commit because all three edit `tests/integration/test_i_29_m9.py`.
  **Why:** these are the fixes the issues name.
  **Issue:** #838, #839, #840
- **Blocker:** #841. When every non-player is benched, a structured turn gives 422 `player_has_no_context`; the Executor simulation's call is "all-benched turns still run". Running it means a narrator-only structured turn (no render), a new turn path (Rule 4 territory). Keeping the 422 means correcting the planner line and docs. The options and a recommendation (B: keep the 422 and document it) are on the issue, which is labelled `blocked` + `needs-owner-action`. Nothing else in the pass depends on it.
  **Issue:** #841
- **Decision (owner, 2026-11-10):** #841 takes option B. A structured turn with every non-player benched stays 422 `validation_error` (`player_has_no_context`), as in a structured story whose only character is the player. FR-MULTI-13 (docs/03) now states the all-benched rule for both profiles: Lite renders the player, structured gives 422. docs/04's I-31 gains the case and its Lite complement. `test_i_31__m9_all_benched` asserts both, with no model call and nothing written on the refusal. No product code changed. The Executor simulation's "all-benched turns still run" and #831's "it is not an error" are superseded for structured stories.
  **Why:** the owner's answer on the blocker. Option A would have needed a narrator-only structured turn path.
  **Issue:** #841

## /n8-exec M9 fix pass 2 — 2026-11-11

- **Decision:** the pass runs on `milestone/m9-verify-fixes-2` in the worktree `.claude/worktrees/m9fix2`, off `origin/main` at 7e7083c, in this session (four small issues). The local check was ruff, format, mypy, lint-imports and the touched modules' tests: `tests/gates`, I-29 (M9), C-02, C-03, the registry, the Lite prompt, terminology and S-erasure-boundary, 764 passed. CI's sharded run on the PR is the full-suite gate, as in the earlier M9 runs.
  **Why:** the main checkout holds the owner's `m8-e11-evidence` branch and uncommitted `.idea` edits. The full local suite takes about 10 hours.
  **Issue:** M9 (#14)
- **Decision:** the plan comments on #847–#850 were posted after the code was written, not before it. Their content is what was built.
  **Why:** a process slip, recorded here.
  **Issue:** #847, #848, #849, #850
- **Decision (Rule 1):** the scan takes each attribute-reading filter's name position from Jinja's own signature (`ATTRIBUTE_POSITIONS`, derived with `inspect` at import: every built-in filter with an `attribute` parameter, plus `selectattr`/`rejectattr` at 0). `test_i_29__m9_valid_edges` pins the derived map, so a Jinja upgrade that moves a position fails a test.
  **Why:** the derivation found `join(d, attribute)`, which #837's hand list and #847 both missed: `join(',', '_y')` read a `_` key at render. A derived map cannot drift from the filters the environment actually runs.
  **Issue:** #847
- **Decision (Rule 1):** beyond the shapes #847 lists, the scan now refuses the rest of the same class, each found by a probe on 7e7083c that read a `_` key at render. These are:
  - `.format`/`.format_map` wherever named, a bound one taken without a call included;
  - `.get` with a `_` or computed key, or taken without a call;
  - a `%` whose left side is a constant with a `_`-prefixed `%(name)` field, or a computed format with a right side that could be a mapping (`x % 2`, `'%s' % x` and `'%(voter)s' % inputs` stay accepted);
  - the `format` filter with a `_` keyword;
  - `*args`/`**kwargs` on any filter, test or call (before, only on the attribute filters);
  - `map('<filter>', …)`, checked as that filter with the remaining arguments, so nested `map('map', 'attr', …)` and `map('sum', '_y')` are caught; a computed filter name is refused.
  **Why:** FR-MODEL-14's rule is "reads an attribute or item whose name starts with `_`", checked at save. #837's lesson was that each route left open gets reported one verify at a time.
  **Issue:** #847
- **Decision:** dumping a whole mapping (`tojson`, `items`, `dictsort`, `pprint`, `xmlattr`, iteration) stays accepted, though it shows `_` keys of the caller's inputs.
  **Why:** none of these names an attribute or item. FR-MODEL-14 refuses reading by a `_` name, and the inputs are the caller's own data.
  **Issue:** #847
- **Decision:** `orchestrator/models/consumer.py` still re-runs `check_template` when it resolves a stored version. A version saved before this pass that uses a newly refused form now fails at call time.
  **Why:** the re-check is the existing safety net, and no release has shipped since M7, so only local data is affected (as #848 noted for #837).
  **Issue:** #847
- **Decision:** #849's fail-first mutants are out-of-tree pytest plugins on `orchestrator.purposes.story.render_viewpoint`:
  - a leak to every viewpoint;
  - a leak to Cato only;
  - a viewpoint with its private, retrieved and working memories emptied.
  Each fails the new test, and the old test passes under all three. The test gains a complement: Briar's context lacks the marker before the write.
  **Why:** the first leak mutant trips the new pre-write complement before Cato's check, so the Cato-only one shows that Cato's assertion bites on its own. My first pair of mutants returned a string where `render_viewpoint` returns a `Viewpoint`, and they failed for that reason. They were rewritten, and their results were not counted.
  **Issue:** #849
- **Decision:** #850's case is a new test, `test_i_29__m9_story_character_policy`, with one policy scoped to Briar on both `text_input` and `text_output`. Its mutants patch `story.prepare_story`:
  - whole cast as render targets, with the scoped character as actor;
  - whole cast on output only;
  - no actor.
  Each fails it.
  **Why:** one policy on both targets proves the input and output boundaries with one setup. The output-only mutant fails at the reason check, because the refused output's retry returns the stub default; that is why the test asserts the output text.
  **Issue:** #850

- **Decision (Rule 1):** a constant string key is checked as the attribute Jinja may fall back to:
  - `['format']` and `['format_map']` are refused outright, as `.format` is. This also refuses an input key literally named `format`, and that is accepted because `.format` was already refused.
